caribbean.title: antigua to st lucia
intro: Both are jewels in the crown of the Caribbean, but this yacht charter from Antigua to St Lucia offers the best of both worlds. Embarking on this journey allows you to answer the age-old question: Antigua or St Lucia? Experience the serene beauty and luxuries of the Leeward Islands.

The stunning Leeward islands of the Caribbean provide an excellent opportunity to enjoy a leisurely cruise amidst secluded tranquility. This route from Antigua to St Lucia provides time to really discover some breath-taking places as you explore this incredible yacht charter destination.

With so many different islands, it would take a very long time to fully discover all of the delightful Leeward Islands. Variety abounds with coral reefs, marine parks and swathes of perfect beaches featuring heavily. Antigua or St Lucia? Both are exceptional in their ways. Snorkelling and diving here are sublime as the underwater world is teeming with marine life. The mild climate and cool constant winds in the Leewards offer some of the best blue-water cruising in the world.

stops.heading: antigua to guadeloupe
stops.text: Embark at Falmouth Harbour on the north west side of the western island. Cruise from here to Guadaloupe and find a sheltered anchorage of choice, where you can enjoy views of the surrounding mountains, lush rain forests and vibrant towns. This is a great area for snorkeling with colourful underwater life amidst crystalline waters. Guadeloupe’s two main islands form the shape of butterfly wings, joined only by bridges and a mangrove swamp. Grand Terre has fabulous beaches teaming with activities and Basse Terre is home to the Parc National, boasting the incredible La Soufriere volcano. Overnight at Deshais Harbour.

stops.heading: guadeloupe
stops.text: In the morning, make way to Isles des Saint’s, a group of islands on the southern end of Guadeloupe with a choice of 2 main anchorages. There is Bourg des Saints on the main island in front of the town and shops, or alternatively, Islet a Cabrit offers a quieter, sheltered anchorage on one of the smaller islands. Both are great places to really enjoy some relaxation while you swim and snorkel the day away.

stops.heading: guadeloupe to dominica
stops.text: Prince Rupert’s Bay is a large natural harbour, set on the northwestern part of the island. It is a great idea to book an organized, guided boat tour up the Indian River surrounded by the rainforest teeming with wildlife. In addition, there is a large town to explore, some great places to snorkel and taking time to simply soak up the atmosphere.

stops.heading: dominica to martinique
stops.text: After breakfast, head to Fort de France for customs clearance then locate a suitable anchorage across from the harbor, near the beach at Anse a L’ane (there is a good choice of places). There are picturesque towns and swathes of velvet beaches ashore. Snorkeling is very good on the outer reefs thanks to the wonderful marine flora and fauna biodiversity.

stops.heading: martinique to st lucia
stops.text: Make way to Marigot Bay and enjoy the sheer tranquility of this beautiful St Lucia yacht charter location. If you head ashore there are some outstanding seafood restaurants or perhaps visit the dive centre at Marigot Beach Club for a fantastic underwater adventure. After lunch, nearby Soufriere, is small town scattered with brightly painted buildings and a bustling seafront. Home to the Diamond Botanical Gardens, this former plantation is bursting with ornamental plants, a waterfall plus geothermal mineral baths. Further inland the cascading Toraille Waterfall is an amazing sight. Anchor overnight near the famous Pitons, which are spectacular volcanic mountain twin peaks.

stops.heading: the pitons to vieux fort
stops.text: Take time to soak up the scenery and explore the Pitons, this world heritage site offers some fantastic walks plus a range of superb diving and snorkeling. Gros Piton, the loftier of the two peaks is climbable for keen hikers and truly affords an ultimate vantage point to view the island. Alternatively, if you are feeling adventurous, a trip by island buggy, a Segway tour or rainforest ziplining can be great fun and will likely cover areas you would not otherwise see. Make way in the evening to Vieux Fort and spend the night in harbour.

stops.heading: vieux fort
stops.text: Situated at the southern end of the island, enjoy the approaching view of mountain ranges and long white sandy beaches plus this area is great for wind and kitesurfing should the mood take you. Perhaps head ashore to Moule a Chique, scenic point, to take advantage of the 360 vistas from this high point. Cruise round to Anse des Sables Beach and drop anchor to enjoy lunch. Disembark at your leisure – Hewanorra International Airport is nearby.

caribbean.title: Nassau to Nassau
intro: With a bewildering choice of seven hundred islands and innumerable cays, these stunning cruising grounds have so much to offer.

Whether you are looking to dive into the beautiful blue depths or enjoy “catch of the day” for lunch at a local beach cafe, this island-strewn archipelago will not disappoint. History enthusiasts,carnival-seekers or those wanting complete relaxation will find what they are looking for in this multi-faceted paradise.

This itinerary brings all perfect ingredients together for a memorable cruise: short passages between destinations, tranquil seclusion, beautiful scenery, fresh seafood and great watersports opportunities. Combine this with sun, breeze and the Bahamas’ colourful character, and this a recipe for success.

stops.heading: Nassau to Compass Cay
stops.text: Cruise from Nassau to Compass Cay (approx. 70nm) where you can swim with the nurse sharks right in the marina or take a stroll down the quaint nature paths to the secluded beach on the other side. The walkway here is painted with colorful buoys and signage along the way giving you a true local feel. From here you can anchor off near Rocky Dundas Caves. These two caves are hidden inside a large rock with natural skylights at the top. In order to enter the cave you must swim into a shallow hole where you end up inside a cavern of stalactites and stalagmites. It is quite awe inspiring. With a mask, snorkel and fins, the sea life surrounding this rock is so colorful and it’s shallow.

stops.heading: Compass cay to staniel cay
stops.text: On to Staniel Cay (10nm) where you can dock at the marina or anchor nearby in several well protected areas. With its handsome stone architecture, good food, and friendly bar, the small but intimate Yacht Club attracts adventurers from around the world. Next door at Sampson and Big Major is home to the native wild pigs which often swim a few yards out to greet you. A must see is “Thunderball Cave” where the fish eat right out of your hand. You may want to dine ashore at Royal Plantation Island at Fowl Cay a private resort island, which is run by ex-yachties.

stops.heading: staniel cay to little bells cay
stops.text: Cruise from Staniel Cay back north to Little Bells Cay / Cambridge Cay for the night (10nm). There is a hidden, shallow cut in between the long stretch of beach where no boat would venture as it does dry up at low tide. Enjoy a swim and let the current carry you through as if riding a small rapid. White sand and crystal blue water is the perfect canvas to see a few small sting rays swim by. A short hike up to the lookout will give you an amazing vantage point of the surrounding islands.

stops.heading: little bells cay to highbourne cay
stops.text: Head from Little Bells to Highbourne Cay and Allan’s Cay (approx. 20nm) to see the famous Iguanas roaming the beach and traverse through this jagged yet beautiful cut. You may opt for a short snorkel around the Norman’s Cay sunken airplane which sits in shallow water not far from this northern spot in the Exuma chain. There is a marina at Highbourne or you can choose to anchor further down in a more protected location. Cruise back to Nassau from Highbourne and if time allows, a quick dip off of Rose Island.

caribbean.title: St Maarten to St Maarten
intro: With a fabulous choice of stunning bays, wonderful marinas and exceptional towns to explore, you will be spoiled for choice during this superyacht charter itinerary.

Cruise calm waters to enjoy an island-hopping adventure in paradise. Whether you seek secluded coves, bustling coastal towns, vibrant nightlife or delicious local cuisine - this itinerary has something for everyone.

stops.heading: simpson bay, st maarten
stops.text: Arrive and be escorted to Marina Isle de Sol, Simpson Bay before sailing to Grande Case to spend the evening at anchor. Before or after your dinner on board, venture ashore for an evening drink. Soak up the French ambiance of a coastal town bustling with cafés and quaint restaurants.

stops.heading: simpson bay to grand case
stops.text: Awake to a full array of yacht toys and enjoy the morning in the bay of Grand Case, where there are no restrictions for waterskiing or jet‐skiing. After lunch on board, your crew will take you to meet a private driver for an afternoon of zip‐lining at Loterie Farm. Then sail the 2 hours to St. Barths for a guided tour of the island, or a leisurely hike up to the old fort to take some photos. Shop in the boutiques or enjoy a day of pampering at one of the magnificent spa’s. Dine at The Eden Roc Hotel before heading to Nikki Beach for drinks.

stops.heading: gustavia
stops.text: After choosing your favourite anchorage in St. Barts and enjoying the warm water, head to the island’s capital, Gustavia, and settle for the night.

stops.heading: st barts to barbuda
stops.text: Head off from St Barths to the island of Barbuda, arriving just in time for lunch. Anchor in Low Bay’s aquamarine waters and explore the endless white sand beaches. After lunch, enjoy a full beach setup with beach games and enjoy the water sports on offer. Enjoy sundowners and sunset views from the jacuzzi on the sundeck.

stops.heading: barbuda to st kitts
stops.text: Sail through the night to St. Kitts and anchor in White House Bay, offering total protection from any weather. Venture ashore or use the water toys available. There is a terrific beach bar at Banana Bay for sundowners.

stops.heading: st kitts
stops.text: Head to shore for a 4x4 off‐road tour, bird tour, railway or rainforest tour. Lunch ashore and then take the tender for an afternoon of offshore fishing. The yacht will then set sail while you sleep, so wake up to a brand new anchorage in Anguilla.

stops.heading: anguilla
stops.text: Awake in Rendezvous Bay, Anguilla. Take advantage of the service of the crew and enjoy beachcombing or hit the beach bars. If there are golfers in your party, this is a great opportunity to play. Anchor in Rendezvous Bay for the night.

stops.heading: st maarten
stops.text: Sail through the night towards St. Maarten, arriving at an anchorage to enjoy the final morning of water sports before returning to dock.

mediterranean.title: Rome to Naples
intro: The Italian Amalfi coastline is a yachting haven, offering a variety of exceptional anchorages, fabulous cuisine, coastal towns and picturesque fishing villages. This is a wonderful location to experience la dolce vita while on a yacht charter.

Entering into Civitavecchia by yacht is special. Rome needs no introduction, tradition, history and culture say it all. Dine in style amidst architecture of days gone by, marvel at the multitude of breath-taking sights and become immersed in the wonderful Italian lifestyle bursting with huge personality.

Steeped in history, the wide Gulf of Naples is a panoramic bay fringed by the islands of Capri, Ischia and Procida, where visitors can discover monuments, sweeping scenery and the classic Italian way of life. Achingly romantic with unique allure, the Amalfi Coast offers an idyllic location, with rugged peaks and clifftop palazzos providing a cinematic backdrop for cruising

stops.heading: rome
stops.text: Impossible to appreciate in just one day, Rome offers an enormous amount to do and see. The Eternal City is deeply complex and vastly sprawling. However just capturing a few of the highlights on a sightseeing tour may be worth planning ahead. The Colosseum and Forum are amongst the most iconic attractions that can easily be viewed. If you throw coins in the Trevi Fountain you’ll be sure to return to explore the delights of Rome in the future. Alternatively coastal Rome has huge appeal with a range of beaches and waterfront entertainment available such as Anzio located slightly south.

stops.heading: ponza
stops.text: Clandestine and inviting, the rugged island of Ponza is a tranquil yachting haven where windless coves dot the coastline. This crescent shaped island rises from the water with rocky hills covered in verdant scrub and brightly coloured houses cluster in quaint towns. Casual restaurants deliver understated aperitifs and delicious fresh fare; this is a place to relish unmitigated Italian charm with laid-back simplicity. Take this opportunity to mess around on the water with THUMPER’s large array of water toys. After a fun-filled day, spend the evening enjoying an al fresco dinner in the company of your guests and watch the beautiful sunset.

stops.heading: ischia
stops.text: Volcanic Ischia is steeped in ancient mythology and famed for its hot thermal springs. The interior boasts lush semi-tropical vegetation with a fascinating mix of vineyards and quirky towns across the landscape. Visit designer boutiques along Via Roma, stroll through the gorgeous Mortella Gardens and relax in traffic-free Sant’Angelo.

stops.heading: capri
stops.text: Small in size, but huge in personality – the exclusive island of Capri is a buzzing, cosmopolitan hub. The playground of discerning Italian gentry, Capri has excellent hotels, restaurants and boutiques. Lively and colourful, whilst also offering spectacular scenery, experience the view from the sheer cliffs of Tiberius’s Leap and visit the natural marvel of the Blue Grotto. Do not miss the sunset at Capri – it is simply breath-taking.

stops.heading: amalfi
stops.text: Make way to the cascading beauty of Amalfi and anchor off Nerano- maybe take lunch at Maria Grazia Restaurant - renowned for spaghetti with zucchini and the friendliness of the owners. Amalfi itself is gracefully picturesque, dotted with clusters of pastel buildings ambling up the hillside. At Cape Conca, the Emerald Grotto is one of Amalfi’s natural wonders. Emitting an eerie emerald hue emanating from its depths thanks to light refracting from an underwater crevice. Hidden coves and sandy bays abound – take time to enjoy the water and simply relaxing in this charming haven.

stops.heading: sorrento
stops.text: With spectacular views over the Bay of Naples, the historic seaside town of Sorrento is packed with picturesque charm. Wander at leisure through the labyrinth of intricate shopping lanes then head to the picturesque fishing quarter at Marina Grande where you can enjoy delicious fresh seafood for lunch on the waterfront. Close to the harbour, the small and sandy beach at Marina Piccola is a popular choice or slightly further south, Punto del Capo, is an attractive option. Adventurous visitors should not pass up a trip to the striking ruins of Vesuvius and Pompeii if time permits

stops.heading: naples
stops.text: Steeped in antiquity, Naples is filled with fascinating culture. The city centre is the largest area of protected history within Europe, spanning 27 centuries. The architecture, monuments and stories that surround this city are simply fascinating. Home of the margherita pizza, stop at one of the bustling restaurants to sample this local delight.

mediterranean.title: Cannes to Monaco
intro: Enjoy cruising the glittering French coastline. Explore market towns, admire architecture, enjoy fine cuisine and soak up the beautiful scenery.

Nowhere else in the world has the concentration of wealth, sophistication and cultural finesse as the Côte d’Azur. Often referred to as the Millionaire’s Mediterranean Playground, here you can put on the glitz, experience the cachet of casinos, visit galleries and taste some of the finest food in the world. Then drop anchor, sip some chilled rosé and watch the sun set over a picturesque mountainous backdrop. Small wonder it’s the place to be seen.

stops.heading: cannes
stops.text: Cannes is the glamorous beating heart of the Cote d’Azur. Natural harbour-side beauty sits sympathetically beside brazen opulence in this highly desirable place to see and be seen. In the sunshine, couture shops and art deco hotels of La Croisette impress with the chic glamour of days gone by. Ferraris and Porsches cruise the strip and celebrity-spotting is easy along striped-lounger private beaches. The palmshaded promenade affords an easy walk whilst revealing open views of the Baie de Cannes and nearby Estérel mountains. Legendary, multi-starred hotels such as the Martinez and the Carlton, renowned for historical visits from an abundance of stars over the years, set a benchmark in exclusive privacy

stops.heading: the lerin islands
stops.text: The Lerins are a group of four tiny islands a short hop from Cannes, well worth visiting to while away the hours. The two main islands are Sainte- Marguerite and Saint-Honorat; the micro islands are Tradelière and St-Féréol. Drop anchor in Plateau du Mileu, the shallow, protected passage between the two main islands and visit the nearest and largest: luscious Ile Sainte Marguerite is smothered in a carpet of fragrant Allepo pine and eucalyptus with wide pathways artistically criss-crossing the island. Bring nets and snorkelling gear - bursting with tiny rocky bays it’s a great place for rockpooling and crabbing with younger travellers, with just one long sandy beach in this haven of calm with no traffic.

stops.heading: antibes
stops.text: The thriving superyacht port of Antibes, encircled by ancient stone walls, exudes a relaxed beachy feel backed by a gorgeous old town with narrow cobbled streets, markets and thriving café culture. If you want to combine great beaches, culture, history and good food, Antibes will match your needs. Traditional and bustling, Port Vauban is the largest marina in Europe, where a selection of the biggest and most glamorous yachts afloat anchor during the summer months. The old town is a warren of quaint cafes, bars and boutiques with a busy Provençal market where wafts of fragrant lavender mixed with ripe local cheeses drift in the air.

stops.heading: nice
stops.text: A globally renowned tourist destination, Nice epitomises the French Mediterranean with seashores, mountains and architecture all with equal appeal. Bustling with life, stroll the streets to enjoy infectious cafe culture whilst taking time to admire the Belle Epoque architecture and Baroque houses.

stops.heading: st jean cap ferrat
stops.text: Providing a great anchorage, St Jean Cap Ferrat, near Villefranche, is a ragged headland where substantial private homes are just visible from the water. Enjoying a position in the centre of the French Riviera, between Monaco and Nice, Cap Ferrat is notable for its clutch of exclusive hotels, restaurants and beach clubs, and ideally placed for quick access to many destinations all along the Cote d’Azur. Long, languid days can be spent swimming off the back deck, diving in the incredible waters and snoozing on the beaches – themselves a catwalk of beauty and glamour.

stops.heading: eze
stops.text: The perched village of Eze, with it's clusters of houses atop rocky cliffs, commands incredible views. One of the most celebrated French Riviera resorts, situated at an altitude of 426m above sea level, the old village is a maze of narrow, winding streets and shady squares. At the very top the ruined castle of Eza boasts stunning botanical gardens set on the steep slopes - simply perfect to wander and soak up the views.

stops.heading: monaco
stops.text: The principality of Monaco is the world’s second smallest country, making up for its size with immense personality. Sitting atop a narrow coastal area with three sides bounded by France and facing the dazzling Mediterranean, it is an inexcusably thrilling destination. One of the most beautiful harbours set against dramatic cliffs and brimming with mega-yachts exudes an aura of exclusive elegance. High-end shopping, luxurious hotels and five casinos are all skilfully condensed into an area just 1.25 square miles to top off the intoxicating allure of Monaco.

mediterranean.title: calvi to cala di volpe
intro: Experience the high-life amongst these gorgeous hotspots of the Western Mediterranean, where pretty coastlines and fine dining offer the perfect Italian-French mix for an unforgettable charter.

Modern and elegant, a yacht charter in Corsica and Sardinia is a chic affair: indeed combining both fabulous islands brings about the best of both worlds. Rugged Corsica is an absolute delight with an undulating coastline strewn with fishing villages and sheer beauty at the Scandola Nature Reserve. In addition, Sardinia’s white sand beaches peppered with trendy beach clubs belie the inland riches of fascinating ancient cities and Michelin-starred restaurant.
An itinerary here is a photographer’s paradise: make the most of exceptional panoramic views, many-hues of azure water and architecture to make you step back in time.

stops.heading: calvi to girolata
stops.text: Calvi’s marina is a perfect starting point for your trip, where the dedicated crew members will welcome you on board. A gentle cruise to Golfe of Girolata, a stunning nature reserve with romantic flair, is a lovely setting to enjoy your first afternoon and evening.

stops.heading: girolata - ajaccio
stops.text: Move towards the fascinating birthplace of Napoleon, where you can enjoy a walk through the beautiful old town and discover the scenic ruins of Ajaccio.

stops.heading: ajaccio - bonifacio
stops.text: Head towards the lively, medieval town of Bonifacio after enjoying some entertaining water sports in the morning. This miniature St Tropez has sights to see, streets to stroll and restaurants in which you will find excellent Mediterranean cuisine. Built on eroded limestone, Bonifacio has simply amazing views out to sea.

stops.heading: bonifacio - maddalena islands
stops.text: Cruise to the La Maddalena archipelago, to the north of Sardinia, where an unspoiled area of outstanding natural beauty awaits. Take the tender and explore the little coves and bays: the water here is among the most striking in the West Med.

stops.heading: maddalena islands - porto cervo
stops.text: Anchoring at Porto Cervo, take the opportunity to shop in some chic and exclusive boutiques. Enjoy the sunset with a cocktail whilst watching the world go by before dining at one of the excellent restaurants along the promenade. Don’t forget to dress for the occasion.

stops.heading: porto cervo - cala di volpe
stops.text: Unspoiled beaches call out for swimming while the warm sand is ideal for sunbathing. The bay of Cala di Volpe is perfect for complete and utter relaxation, finished off by drinks and dinner at the Yacht Club Costa Smeralda.

stops.heading: cala di volpe - porto rotondo
stops.text: End your superyacht charter at picturesque Porto Rotondo, where you have the chance to have a last alfresco dinner on board.

antarctica/antarctica.title: Antarctica Itinerary
intro: The startling white continent of Antarctica, strewn with shimmering blue bergs and home to incredible wildlife, is a dream destination for adventurous yacht charterers seeking the ultimate voyage of discovery.

To afford more time on your Antarctica yacht charter adventure, and avoid the two day sail across the notorious Drake Passage, take a flight from Punta Arenas to land at King George Island (South Shetland). Here you can embark your expedition vessel.

Executing a successful itinerary on your Antarctica yacht charter requires flexibility, as you'll need to work with the prevailing ice and weather conditions to determine the best and safest route. Expedition leaders will inform and guide you every step of the way with presentations and briefings, sharing their detailed knowledge of this region. The following is just an outline of what is possible during a voyage in the Antarctic.

stops.heading: punta arenas to king george island
stops.text: Board your flight (timing will be weather dependant) from Punta Arenas to King George Island. Landing at the airstrip, there will be a quick opportunity to visit Russia's Bellinghausen base nearby. Transfer to the waterfront and board the Zodiac tenders to board your expedition vessel for your Antarctica yacht charter. Here you will be briefed on the safety and landing procedures by guides and leaders whilst also acquainting yourself with the crew and new surroundings.

stops.heading: the southern shetland islands
stops.text: Stretching at the very northern tip of Antarctica, on the edge of the Drake Passage, the South Sheltland Islands are rich with wildlife. Penguin colonies, seabirds and seals live on and around the isles. With a detailed history from sealing and whaling, they are also where most of the research stations are located and you will be able to visit some of these as you discover the islands.

stops.heading: deception island
stops.text: As the flooded caldera of a volcano, having last erupted in the '70s, Deception Island is packed with exciting geology and more. Home to the region's largest chinstrap penguin colonies, the island has a history of shore-based whaling. Warmed slightly by the hot rocks below, this is apparently the warmest place for a swim in the Antarctic.

stops.heading: antarctic sound
stops.text: Affectionately known as Iceberg Alley, Antarctic Sound lives up to its nickname, with drifting chunks of iceberg flowing north from the Weddell Sea. On Paulet Island or Devil Island, take time to visit the Adelié penguin colonies. On the east side are the northern areas of the Weddell Sea. On Snow Hill Island look out for the emperor penguins who breed here in the winter months. During the summer, the colonies dissipate, however you may see newly fledged chicks sitting on the ice.

stops.heading: the danco coast & gerlache strait
stops.text: Head west and spend a couple of days exploring a variety of islands and passages in this stunning region during your Antarctica yacht charter. Visiting the gentoo penguin colonies is very entertaining and there are some nearby active research stations too. There is a wide variety of amazing experiences waiting to be discovered, all depending upon prevailing weather conditions.

stops.heading: south shetland to punta arenas
stops.text: The vessel will return to South Shetland and anchor off King George island, in order to meet your flight back to Punta Arenas (weather depending). It is recommended to plan for an overnight in Punta Arenas and onward travel home for the next day due to the overall uncertainty of exact flight times.

antarctica/antarctica.teaser: The startling white continent of Antarctica, strewn with shimmering blue bergs and home to incredible wildlife, provides adventurous yacht charterers with the ultimate voyage of discovery.

arctic/east-greenland.title: East Greenland
intro: East Greenland supplies an unparalleled blend of breathtaking natural beauty and thrilling exploration.
Whether you’re drawn to the awe-inspiring Northern Lights, the abundance of wildlife, or discovering some of the world’s most remote destinations, this region promises an unforgettable adventure.

Experience the ethereal glow of the aurora borealis during the winter months or enjoy the endless daylight of summer, when the sun never sets, both of these seasons reveal the true magic of East Greenland. Whether you’re weaving through giant icebergs or admiring the natural ice sculptures that make this region famous, this trip is certain to exceed your expectations.

stops.heading: Constable Point
stops.text: Your journey begins as you depart from Keflavik Airport and fly to Nerlerit Inaat Airport, also known as Constable Point. This iconic location is admired for its dramatic landscapes and crystal-clear skies, offering a rare opportunity for stargazing and witnessing the mesmerising Northern Lights. Here, your charter adventure begins, setting the stage for an extraordinary exploration.

stops.heading: Viking Bay To Danmark Island
stops.text: Viking Bay, a stunning destination rich in history and natural beauty, is home to some of the world’s most well-preserved Viking ruins. Surrounded by impressive peaks, this area allows you to and some of the deep history that this area is so famed for. You’ll also visit Danmark Island, where the rock formations are covered in a blanket of vibrant foliage. This area is a haven for wildlife, so keep your camera ready. Here, you may spot seals, Arctic foxes, white-tailed eagles, and even humpback whales.

stops.heading: Hare Fjord, Ofjord, Bear Island, Sydkap
stops.text: Set sail through the stunning Hare Fjord, believed to be named after the Arctic hare, where you’ll enjoy panoramic views of towering mountains with snow-capped peaks. Next, explore Ofjord, part of Scoresby Sound, the world’s longest fjord system. Sail through natural ice arches before making your way to Bear Islands, where the panoramic views of the waterways are simply unmatched.

stops.heading: Thule Remains & Northeast Greenland National Park
stops.text: Continuing your journey, you’ll visit the Thule Remains and Northeast Greenland National Park, the world’s largest national park and a place of immense beauty. Here you’re likely to spot some of the diverse animals that call this national park home. This includes the snowy owl, collared lemming, bearded seal, Arctic hare and Greenland wolves, a small pack that plays a crucial role in maintaining the Arctic ecosystem.

stops.heading: Ittoqqortoormiit
stops.text: Ittoqqortoormiit has been named one of the world’s most remote settlements and has a population of just 400 people. Surrounded by towering mountains, this colourful destination offers a unique opportunity for visitors to experience what it is like to live in such a secluded yet undeniably beautiful corner of the world. Here, you’ll be able to embark on a tour of Ittoqqortoormiit, hosted by a local guide who is native to this settlement, providing visitors with an inside look into how this remote community thrives.

arctic/east-greenland.teaser: East Greenland supplies an unparalleled blend of breathtaking natural beauty and thrilling exploration. Whether you’re drawn to the awe-inspiring Northern Lights, the abundance of wildlife, or discovering some of the world’s most remote destinations, this region promises an unforgettable adventure.

arctic/svalbard.title: Longyearbyen to Longyearbyen
intro: Discover one of the world’s most extraordinary destinations on an exclusive expedition to Svalbard, a remote Arctic archipelago renowned for its untamed beauty, abundant wildlife, and dramatic landscapes.

This exclusive ten-day voyage takes you from Longyearbyen through the western, northern, and eastern fjords of Spitsbergen, navigating remote waters and pristine ice fields that lead toward the North Pole. Svalbard is a land of rugged wilderness where majestic glaciers meet the sea, reindeer roam the mountainsides, and elusive polar bears can sometimes be seen along the ice edge. This itinerary offers a rare and intimate perspective on the Arctic‘s breathtaking landscapes.

Svalbard’s most awe-inspiring sights, from peaceful landings at untouched fjords to wilderness hikes and zodiac tours along the ice floes are all on the menu. Discover spectacular bird cliffs, explore the uninhabited island of Prins Karls Forland, and cruise through waters rich in marine life. For the discerning adventurer, this voyage promises an unparalleled connection with nature, providing the finest standards of comfort and service on board as you encounter one of Earth’s last true frontiers.

stops.heading: Longyearbyen - Western Fjords
stops.text: Begin your adventure in Longyearbyen. In the afternoon, embark on the expedition vessel after an introduction from the expedition leader and a safety briefing from the Captain. Then, set sail out through the Adventfjord and wave goodbye to civilisation.

stops.heading: Western Fjords
stops.text: In the morning, sail by Prins Karls Forland, an uninhabited island of beautiful scenery off the west coast of Spitsbergen. This is a place where sometimes walruses are likely to haul out or be sighted. In the afternoon, perhaps get your boots on for a hike to spot grazing reindeer. If the conditions allow, sail along the coast exploring places such as Krossfjorden, home to majestic glaciers, and some of Svalbard’s most beautiful fjords and scenery.

stops.heading: Western Fjords - Northern Fjords & Ice Edge
stops.text: Over the next few days, navigate between the coast and the sea ice that extends all the way to the North Pole. Count on regular shore landings and zodiac tours to visit different natural and historical sites including glaciers and partake in wilderness hikes.

stops.heading: Northern Fjords & Ice Edge - East Coast
stops.text: If sea ice allows, head east towards the Hinlopen Strait, exploring ice, cliffs, and crossing the 80° North parallel. Long days will be filled with adventure, zodiac cruises, wildlife spotting, and vast bird cliffs. Depending on the ice and winds, either continue south or turn back west.

stops.heading: East Coast - Southern Fjords
stops.text: Head south along Spitsbergen’s coast, visiting rarely explored landing sites and enjoying the breathtaking nature and wildlife. After rounding the southern tip, explore Hornsund with wilderness hikes before sailing north toward Isfjorden.

stops.heading: Southern Fjords - Isfjorden
stops.text: Already back in the protection of Isfjorden, find peaceful landing sites to hike or simply relax and take it all in. Isfjorden offers a fantastic mix of landscapes, history and wildlife, offering the best possible closure to the experience before heading back to civilisation.

stops.heading: Isfjorden - Longyearbyen
stops.text: By morning, arrive back at the port of Longyearbyen. Disembark the ship and say goodbye to the new friends you’ve made, all the while keeping the memories of the transformative adventure you shared together.

arctic/svalbard.teaser: Discover one of the world’s most extraordinary destinations on an exclusive expedition to Svalbard, a remote Arctic archipelago renowned for its untamed beauty, abundant wildlife, and dramatic landscapes.

australia-and-new-zealand/australia.title: The Kimberley
intro: Travel around the north-western edge of Australia to discover a raw, wild coastline dotted with some 2600 beautiful islands. The Kimberley, tucked away in the faraway north-west pocket of Australia, is one of the most pristine regions in the world.
Brimming with Australia’s best outback scenery and wildlife, inhabited by just over 50,000 people over 400,000km2, this region is one of the most secluded and scarcely populated in the world.

Reputed as one of Australia’s great natural wonders, discover a never-ending haven of turquoise waters, white sands, waterfalls, and sandstone gorges that will take your breath away. Witness landscapes that have been carved over millions of years, immersed in the diverse wildlife and serenity of the region. Despite the remoteness, this is also a place of great cuisine, friendly locals and one of the most romantic beach towns in the world.

stops.heading: cygnet bay & buccaneer archipelago
stops.text: Your Kimberley adventure starts with a cruise through the islands of King Sound. Take a tender excursion to the Buccaneer Archipelago to witness the ‘giant tides’ where you can watch spectacular whirlpools and overflows being produced. After the exciting tour, head back on board for some relaxing with a cocktail on deck to enjoy your first stunning Kimberley sunset.

stops.heading: king sound to silver gull creek
stops.text: Depart from Cygnet Bay early and cruise across King Sound to uninhabited Hidden Island. Anchor off Silica Beach, one of a kind in The Kimberley, this beach is made from pure, white silica sand making it powder-soft. Spend time here swimming in the turquoise waters and exploring the coastline. At sunset cruise on to your overnight anchorage at the tranquil and remote Silver Gull Creek. Taking dinner on deck, look out for shooting stars in the vast open sky.

stops.heading: cockatoo island to the horizontal falls
stops.text: In the morning cruise past Cockatoo and Koolan Island, both of which are famed for their rich, high grade iron ore, clearly marked by the mining operations that have been established here for decades. Continue to Talbot Bay and head on to the Horizontal Falls which is one of the most breath-taking natural wonders in the Kimberley. Millions of litres of ocean are sucked through a narrow sea gorge at the mouth, where tides as high as 13m push through the two rusty red craggy walls. Affectionately named “Horries”, this natural phenomenon is unlike any other waterfall, as here the water passes horizontally through the narrow gorges. This is a thrilling ride in a fast tender in the Kimberley, indeed travelling with the flow the water surges so fast it goes downhill! Make way to Talbot Bay for an even more powerful natural creation – Cyclone Creek. The rocks are twisted and buckled, displaying spectacular geology in warped horizontal layers. Despite areas of swirling water, the coral reefs are abundant and look out for the ghostly-pale Tawny Nurse Sharks who regularly visit. Back at the yacht, enjoy sunset in Talbot Bay, your anchorage for the night.

stops.heading: montgomery reef to raft point
stops.text: Journey to Montgomery Reef, a dramatic sight, as the “invisible” reef slowly emerges from the ocean on the falling tide. There is often 10m difference on a single tide, so nearly 5m of reef is gradually exposed within about 2 hours from the ocean, with waterfalls and rivers cutting through the reef. Explore up close and watch sea turtles, sea snakes and dolphins playing in the reef and the several small islands nearby are filled with mangroves, crocodiles and bird life. Cruise to Raft Point for an overnight anchorage. This large formation of ochre sandstone is close to the mouth of Doubtful bay.

stops.heading: raft point
stops.text: Head ashore at Raft Point to visit the cave gallery of spectacular Wandjinas – an array of amazing indigenous rock art. Created hundreds of years ago, your local Aboriginal guide will share fascinating stories with you. During the afternoon, take the tender to Scotties Creek. Head ashore for a walk through the lush rainforest and enjoy swimming in one of the beautiful lagoons there. Return to the yacht for a relaxed sunset and spend overnight at the Raft Point anchorage

stops.heading: raft point to boondook bay
stops.text: An early departure from Raft Point means a morning cruising through spectacular coastal scenery. Make way back towards Boondook Bay where the yacht will anchor for a leisurely lunch. Take the tenders for an afternoon of exploring the islands and coastline or perhaps relax on board, soaking up the sun. Overnight anchorage in Boondook Bay.

stops.heading: boondook bay to cygnet bay
stops.text: Cruise across King Sound and head back to Cygnet Bay. Along the way keep your eyes open for whales and dolphins. Enjoy a final delicious lunch in the gorgeous surroundings of Cygnet Bay. Transfer ashore for ongoing transport.

stops.heading: Felicite Island
stops.text: The amazing resort island of Felicité is a wonderful location for another action packed day of watersports. This lush, granite isle is just a short tender ride from one of the best snorkelling spots in the world where the abundant marine life is fascinating. The luxurious Six Senses private island resort is an idyllic ecological sanctuary, where relaxation is key. From exquisite dining to spa treatments, this is a great spot to indulge in perfect relaxation on powder-white sands.

stops.heading: fregate island
stops.text: Cruise for three hours overnight to spend the last day experiencing the charm of Anse Victorin on the private island resort of Fregate Island. Although small, this beach is simply perfect and no wonder it has been awarded the title of most beautiful beach in the world multiple times. From here surfing with onboard instructors, a last dive or even catching that last tuna is the goal. Take a leisurely four hour cruise back to the main island of Mahé, which can be timed for departure, or enjoy a day back in Saint Anne Marine nature park before heading home.

australia-and-new-zealand/australia.teaser: Travel around the north-western edge of Australia to discover a raw, wild coastline dotted with some 2600 beautiful islands; welcome to The Kimberley.

australia-and-new-zealand/new-zealand.title: Bay of Islands
intro: Unearth the majestic beauty of New Zealand with our 8-day luxury yacht charter New Zealand itinerary. The ideal way to explore the charming coastal towns, steeped in history, and lush islands amidst azure seas, is undoubtedly by a luxury yacht. These islands are achingly beautiful, with silvery beaches lining rocky shores, and pods of dolphins playfully splashing offshore. The peaceful and pristine Bay of Islands, an ideal destination for a yacht charter, are a true gem for relaxed cruising.

Home to 144 islands, ranging from craggy islets to large inhabited isles, the Bay of Islands is situated in the "winterless north" of New Zealand. Partaking in a New Zealand luxury yacht charter, you'll enjoy a mild climate, thanks to tropical currents travelling down from the equator, ensuring the water temperatures are equally pleasant.

On this fabulous luxury yacht charter New Zealand itinerary, start in the Coromandel and head towards the Bay of Islands to stay in more secluded areas. With your Bay of Islands yacht charter, you will have the opportunity to indulge in Northland's finest - fishing, diving, surfing, and sailing. Explore the plethora of marine life, gorgeous stretches of beach, verdant forests, and enjoy the unique charm of local villages ashore.

stops.heading: auckland to coromandel
stops.text: Embark on your New Zealand luxury yacht charter by flying from Auckland International on a private charter plane (approximately 45 minutes), landing on the verdant grass runway of Whitianga Regional Airport. From the marina, travel by tender to your luxury yacht, anchored in Cooks Bay. Settle in and savour lunch on board. Spend your afternoon exploring the scenic Cooks Beach and Cathedral Cove. Surfing enthusiasts will find a great break at Hot Water Beach (weather permitting). As the day ends, sail around to Opito Bay for an overnight anchorage.

stops.heading: opito bay to port charles
stops.text: Start the second day of your Bay of Islands yacht charter with a leisurely breakfast, followed by an exhilarating dive for scallops. Indulge in a lunch of freshly caught seafood, the best of New Zealand's bounty. Cruise to the picturesque Great Mercury Island and Peach Grove Bay for a scenic stop. Your afternoon could be spent exploring rocky dive sites for lobster or snapper fishing around Great Mercury. Conclude your day with a sail to Port Charles to anchor for the night.

stops.heading: broken islands to port fitzroy
stops.text: Day three of your luxury yacht charter in New Zealand begins with a sail across the Colville Channel to Bowling Alley Bay, where you can explore ashore or swim in the warm waters. In the afternoon, cruise the Broken Islands, which truly resemble chunks torn off the land and cast into the sea. Navigate the dramatically narrow Man of War Passage and head to Port Fitzroy. A stop at the iconic Smokehouse Bay prepares you for an evening ashore, offering a yachtsman’s haven, accessible only by boat.

stops.heading: port fitzroy to great barrier islands
stops.text: On the fourth day of your yacht charter around Bay of Islands, consider a three-hour hike up Mount Hobson on Great Barrier Island. Enjoy swimming holes en route and marvel at the spectacular views from the top. If the swell is running, Whangapoua Beach is a great option, otherwise, the Eastern anchorages are absolutely stunning to explore.

stops.heading: the poor knights islands
stops.text: In the morning, journey to Tutukaka and the dramatic Poor Knights Islands, filled with excellent diving opportunities alongside local dive operators. The islands, part of a protected marine and nature reserve, are home to over 125 species, making for an unforgettable underwater adventure on your luxury yacht charter in New Zealand.

stops.heading: bay of islands
stops.text: Day six of your yacht charter introduces you to the protected Bay Islands Marine Park. Consider a hike along the Cape Brett Walkway, or visit the Hole in the Rock, an awe-inspiring site for spearfishing. End your day by anchoring in Oke Bay for the night.

stops.heading: robertson island to russell island
stops.text: Awaken to the tranquillity of your luxury yacht charter. Paddleboard the coast or sail around the bay in search of local pods of Bottle Nose Dolphins. After anchoring off the rugged gem of Robertson Island, consider a visit to the historic Grand Old Duke of Marlborough Pub in Russell.

stops.heading: kerikeri
stops.text: End your 8-day luxury yacht charter in New Zealand in Kerikeri Inlet, famed for its vibrant horticulture and bustling farmer's market. Browse local art galleries and enjoy fresh local produce. At Doves Bay, disembark from your superyacht for onward transport to the Bay of Islands Airport.

australia-and-new-zealand/new-zealand.teaser: Unearth the majestic beauty of New Zealand with our 8-day luxury yacht charter New Zealand itinerary.

caribbean/leeward-islands.title: St Maarten to St Maarten
intro: With a fabulous choice of stunning bays, wonderful marinas and exceptional towns to explore, you will be spoiled for choice during this superyacht charter itinerary.

Cruise calm waters to enjoy an island-hopping adventure in paradise. Whether you seek secluded coves, bustling coastal towns, vibrant nightlife or delicious local cuisine - this itinerary has something for everyone.

stops.heading: simpson bay, st maarten
stops.text: Arrive and be escorted to Marina Isle de Sol, Simpson Bay before sailing to Grande Case to spend the evening at anchor. Before or after your dinner on board, venture ashore for an evening drink. Soak up the French ambiance of a coastal town bustling with cafés and quaint restaurants.

stops.heading: simpson bay to grand case
stops.text: Awake to a full array of yacht toys and enjoy the morning in the bay of Grand Case, where there are no restrictions for waterskiing or jet‐skiing. After lunch on board, your crew will take you to meet a private driver for an afternoon of zip‐lining at Loterie Farm. Then sail the 2 hours to St. Barths for a guided tour of the island, or a leisurely hike up to the old fort to take some photos. Shop in the boutiques or enjoy a day of pampering at one of the magnificent spa’s. Dine at The Eden Roc Hotel before heading to Nikki Beach for drinks.

stops.heading: gustavia
stops.text: After choosing your favourite anchorage in St. Barts and enjoying the warm water, head to the island’s capital, Gustavia, and settle for the night.

stops.heading: st barts to barbuda
stops.text: Head off from St Barths to the island of Barbuda, arriving just in time for lunch. Anchor in Low Bay’s aquamarine waters and explore the endless white sand beaches. After lunch, enjoy a full beach setup with beach games and enjoy the water sports on offer. Enjoy sundowners and sunset views from the jacuzzi on the sundeck.

stops.heading: barbuda to st kitts
stops.text: Sail through the night to St. Kitts and anchor in White House Bay, offering total protection from any weather. Venture ashore or use the water toys available. There is a terrific beach bar at Banana Bay for sundowners.

stops.heading: st kitts
stops.text: Head to shore for a 4x4 off‐road tour, bird tour, railway or rainforest tour. Lunch ashore and then take the tender for an afternoon of offshore fishing. The yacht will then set sail while you sleep, so wake up to a brand new anchorage in Anguilla.

stops.heading: anguilla
stops.text: Awake in Rendezvous Bay, Anguilla. Take advantage of the service of the crew and enjoy beachcombing or hit the beach bars. If there are golfers in your party, this is a great opportunity to play. Anchor in Rendezvous Bay for the night.

stops.heading: st maarten
stops.text: Sail through the night towards St. Maarten, arriving at an anchorage to enjoy the final morning of water sports before returning to dock.

caribbean/leeward-islands.teaser: With a fabulous choice of stunning bays, wonderful marinas and exceptional towns to explore, you will be spoiled for choice during this superyacht charter itinerary.

caribbean/leeward-islands.title: antigua to st lucia
intro: Both are jewels in the crown of the Caribbean, but this yacht charter from Antigua to St Lucia offers the best of both worlds. Embarking on this journey allows you to answer the age-old question: Antigua or St Lucia? Experience the serene beauty and luxuries of the Leeward Islands.

The stunning Leeward islands of the Caribbean provide an excellent opportunity to enjoy a leisurely cruise amidst secluded tranquility. This route from Antigua to St Lucia provides time to really discover some breath-taking places as you explore this incredible yacht charter destination.

With so many different islands, it would take a very long time to fully discover all of the delightful Leeward Islands. Variety abounds with coral reefs, marine parks and swathes of perfect beaches featuring heavily. Antigua or St Lucia? Both are exceptional in their ways. Snorkelling and diving here are sublime as the underwater world is teeming with marine life. The mild climate and cool constant winds in the Leewards offer some of the best blue-water cruising in the world.

stops.heading: antigua to guadeloupe
stops.text: Embark at Falmouth Harbour on the north west side of the western island. Cruise from here to Guadaloupe and find a sheltered anchorage of choice, where you can enjoy views of the surrounding mountains, lush rain forests and vibrant towns. This is a great area for snorkeling with colourful underwater life amidst crystalline waters. Guadeloupe’s two main islands form the shape of butterfly wings, joined only by bridges and a mangrove swamp. Grand Terre has fabulous beaches teaming with activities and Basse Terre is home to the Parc National, boasting the incredible La Soufriere volcano. Overnight at Deshais Harbour.

stops.heading: guadeloupe
stops.text: In the morning, make way to Isles des Saint’s, a group of islands on the southern end of Guadeloupe with a choice of 2 main anchorages. There is Bourg des Saints on the main island in front of the town and shops, or alternatively, Islet a Cabrit offers a quieter, sheltered anchorage on one of the smaller islands. Both are great places to really enjoy some relaxation while you swim and snorkel the day away.

stops.heading: guadeloupe to dominica
stops.text: Prince Rupert’s Bay is a large natural harbour, set on the northwestern part of the island. It is a great idea to book an organized, guided boat tour up the Indian River surrounded by the rainforest teeming with wildlife. In addition, there is a large town to explore, some great places to snorkel and taking time to simply soak up the atmosphere.

stops.heading: dominica to martinique
stops.text: After breakfast, head to Fort de France for customs clearance then locate a suitable anchorage across from the harbor, near the beach at Anse a L’ane (there is a good choice of places). There are picturesque towns and swathes of velvet beaches ashore. Snorkeling is very good on the outer reefs thanks to the wonderful marine flora and fauna biodiversity.

stops.heading: martinique to st lucia
stops.text: Make way to Marigot Bay and enjoy the sheer tranquility of this beautiful St Lucia yacht charter location. If you head ashore there are some outstanding seafood restaurants or perhaps visit the dive centre at Marigot Beach Club for a fantastic underwater adventure. After lunch, nearby Soufriere, is small town scattered with brightly painted buildings and a bustling seafront. Home to the Diamond Botanical Gardens, this former plantation is bursting with ornamental plants, a waterfall plus geothermal mineral baths. Further inland the cascading Toraille Waterfall is an amazing sight. Anchor overnight near the famous Pitons, which are spectacular volcanic mountain twin peaks.

stops.heading: the pitons to vieux fort
stops.text: Take time to soak up the scenery and explore the Pitons, this world heritage site offers some fantastic walks plus a range of superb diving and snorkeling. Gros Piton, the loftier of the two peaks is climbable for keen hikers and truly affords an ultimate vantage point to view the island. Alternatively, if you are feeling adventurous, a trip by island buggy, a Segway tour or rainforest ziplining can be great fun and will likely cover areas you would not otherwise see. Make way in the evening to Vieux Fort and spend the night in harbour.

stops.heading: vieux fort
stops.text: Situated at the southern end of the island, enjoy the approaching view of mountain ranges and long white sandy beaches plus this area is great for wind and kitesurfing should the mood take you. Perhaps head ashore to Moule a Chique, scenic point, to take advantage of the 360 vistas from this high point. Cruise round to Anse des Sables Beach and drop anchor to enjoy lunch. Disembark at your leisure – Hewanorra International Airport is nearby.

caribbean/the-bahamas.title: Nassau to Nassau
intro: With a bewildering choice of seven hundred islands and innumerable cays, these stunning cruising grounds have so much to offer.

Whether you are looking to dive into the beautiful blue depths or enjoy “catch of the day” for lunch at a local beach cafe, this island-strewn archipelago will not disappoint. History enthusiasts,carnival-seekers or those wanting complete relaxation will find what they are looking for in this multi-faceted paradise.

This itinerary brings all perfect ingredients together for a memorable cruise: short passages between destinations, tranquil seclusion, beautiful scenery, fresh seafood and great watersports opportunities. Combine this with sun, breeze and the Bahamas’ colourful character, and this a recipe for success.

stops.heading: Nassau to Compass Cay
stops.text: Cruise from Nassau to Compass Cay (approx. 70nm) where you can swim with the nurse sharks right in the marina or take a stroll down the quaint nature paths to the secluded beach on the other side. The walkway here is painted with colorful buoys and signage along the way giving you a true local feel. From here you can anchor off near Rocky Dundas Caves. These two caves are hidden inside a large rock with natural skylights at the top. In order to enter the cave you must swim into a shallow hole where you end up inside a cavern of stalactites and stalagmites. It is quite awe inspiring. With a mask, snorkel and fins, the sea life surrounding this rock is so colorful and it’s shallow.

stops.heading: Compass cay to staniel cay
stops.text: On to Staniel Cay (10nm) where you can dock at the marina or anchor nearby in several well protected areas. With its handsome stone architecture, good food, and friendly bar, the small but intimate Yacht Club attracts adventurers from around the world. Next door at Sampson and Big Major is home to the native wild pigs which often swim a few yards out to greet you. A must see is “Thunderball Cave” where the fish eat right out of your hand. You may want to dine ashore at Royal Plantation Island at Fowl Cay a private resort island, which is run by ex-yachties.

stops.heading: staniel cay to little bells cay
stops.text: Cruise from Staniel Cay back north to Little Bells Cay / Cambridge Cay for the night (10nm). There is a hidden, shallow cut in between the long stretch of beach where no boat would venture as it does dry up at low tide. Enjoy a swim and let the current carry you through as if riding a small rapid. White sand and crystal blue water is the perfect canvas to see a few small sting rays swim by. A short hike up to the lookout will give you an amazing vantage point of the surrounding islands.

stops.heading: little bells cay to highbourne cay
stops.text: Head from Little Bells to Highbourne Cay and Allan’s Cay (approx. 20nm) to see the famous Iguanas roaming the beach and traverse through this jagged yet beautiful cut. You may opt for a short snorkel around the Norman’s Cay sunken airplane which sits in shallow water not far from this northern spot in the Exuma chain. There is a marina at Highbourne or you can choose to anchor further down in a more protected location. Cruise back to Nassau from Highbourne and if time allows, a quick dip off of Rose Island.

caribbean/the-bahamas.teaser: With an incredible choice of 700 islands and some 2,400 cays, the Bahamas are a rich, varied and idyllic yachting destination.

caribbean/the-bahamas.title: The Florida Keys
intro: Venture into the mesmerizing waters of the Florida Keys aboard our exclusive Florida Keys yacht charter. Located south of Miami, the Florida Keys encompass more than 40 islands, crafting a Florida Keys itinerary that is a mosaic of the best diving and snorkelling spots in the US.

As you embark on this unique private yacht charter in the Florida Keys, you're introduced to North America's only living coral barrier reef. Stretching across 110 miles, the Florida Keys radiate a distinct charm that has made this a top destination for travelers.
Brimming with adventure, sightseeing, and watersports opportunities, the Keys deliver an idyllic yacht charter experience epitomizing luxury and nature's splendor.

stops.heading: biscayne bay & south beach
stops.text: Embark in Miami and settle into your private yacht charter Florida Keys journey. Cruise around Biscayne Bay and along the Intracoastal Waterway, gliding past stunning celebrity mansions and legendary hotels on Fisher Island, Palm Island and Hibiscus Island. Biscayne Bay National Park is a vast marine reserve, extending to the northernmost Keys with reefs, sandbars and iconic Stiltsville, a group of pastel-coloured, stilted huts, only reachable by yacht. Spend the night in harbour at South Beach with the opportunity to experience the best of vibrant Miami nightlife with some of the best bars and nightclubs to be found.

stops.heading: the keys
stops.text: Cruise south towards the Florida Keys on your luxury Florida Keys yacht charter. Along the way, enjoy a variety of watersports such as waterskiing, wakeboarding and diving. Dolphins are often sighted and there may be the chance to snorkel with these gentle mammals. Anglers will also be delighted by the great fishing - the best catches are found out in the open sea with 600 species populating the waters.

stops.heading: key largo
stops.text: The self-proclaimed dive capital of the world, Key Largo has a wealth of diving and snorkeling opportunities on the huge coral reef. If you wish to explore ashore, there are plenty of activities to enjoy, specifically some excellent golfing plus a wide range of shopping and superb restaurants. Two state parks, a national park plus a national marine sanctuary ensure that Key Largo is a wildlife haven. America’s first underwater park - John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park - provides an amazing array of underwater sea life and colourful coral. As the sun sets, tender out to Indian Key, where you can watch the colours fade from the sky on this stunning natural key.

stops.heading: key west
stops.text: In the early morning, cruise to Key West on your private yacht charter in the Florida Keys. Experience the world-famous Keys hospitality on this tropical island getaway. As the southernmost point in the continental US, Key West boasts clear blue skies and fabulous weather. During the day, enjoy watersports and fishing in the azure waters – and head ashore for golf or to visit the Ernest Hemingway Museum. Once the sun sets - get ready to truly begin your Key West experience. Head to Mallory Square for Sunset Celebrations, an impromptu event that just so happens to take place every day of the week! Mingle with musicians, jugglers, and mime artists as you stroll around past sidewalk cafes, open-air bars and elegant restaurants. This cool, funky vibe is what Key West is all about.

stops.heading: the marquesas keys
stops.text: Further west, cruise to the tranquil Marquesas Keys, a circular group of ten uninhabited islands, surrounded by pristine waters, home to corals and mangroves. This is a great opportunity to venture out by kayak and explore the fascinating environment up close on your Florida Keys yacht charter. Spend the afternoon with the water toys and diving wrecks and reefs, before relaxing on deck with a cocktail in hand to watch the notoriously breath-taking sunset.

stops.heading: the keys
stops.text: Starting the return trip on your curated Florida Keys itinerary, enjoy breakfast al fresco to soak up the stunning scenery. Take time out to stop at some of the smaller Keys that were not visited along the way. Cruise past the Saddlebunch Keys – a group of mesmerising mangrove islands, spot Loggerhead turtles nesting at Coco Plum Beach and consider a visit to Islamorada for the diving museum, state park and dolphin encounters.

stops.heading: miami
stops.text: After a leisurely morning cruise, arrive back in the coastal resort of Miami to disembark from your memorable Florida Keys yacht charter. Perhaps conclude your trip with a visit to the Art Deco district of diverse Miami Beach, boasting eclectic architecture and a thriving arts centre.

Alternatively, if you are feeling adventurous, a trip by island buggy, a Segway tour or rainforest ziplining can be great fun and will likely cover areas you would not otherwise see. Make way in the evening to Vieux Fort and spend the night in harbour.

stops.heading: vieux fort
stops.text: Situated at the southern end of the island, enjoy the approaching view of mountain ranges and long white sandy beaches plus this area is great for wind and kitesurfing should the mood take you. Perhaps head ashore to Moule a Chique, scenic point, to take advantage of the 360 vistas from this high point. Cruise round to Anse des Sables Beach and drop anchor to enjoy lunch. Disembark at your leisure – Hewanorra International Airport is nearby.

caribbean/virgin-islands.title: Tortola to Tortola
intro: A yacht charter in the BVI is hard to beat. With over 60 islands in close proximity, it’s an ideal cruising ground for first-time charterers, young families, couples, and seasoned sailors alike.

The shallow waters and short distances between islands allow for easy island hopping, while the BVI’s numerous protected bays provide calm sea conditions even when winds pick up in other Caribbean regions. Whether you’re exploring pristine beaches, indulging in world-class snorkelling and diving, or enjoying a vibrant beach club scene, this 10-day itinerary through the British Virgin Islands offers a mix of relaxation, adventure, and discovery for everyone.

From savouring freshly caught lobster on a secluded beach in Anegada to diving among vibrant coral reefs, each day brings new opportunities to experience the laid-back luxury of the BVI. Thanks to the region’s sheltered waters, you can enjoy smooth cruising throughout your journey, making this a perfect choice for those seeking a seamless island-hopping experience.

stops.heading: Tortola
stops.text: Board your yacht at the picturesque Soper’s Hole Marina. Take a stroll through this colourful harbour, dotted with quaint shops and restaurants like Pusser’s Landing, or venture to Road Town. Here, you can explore the lively streets, sampling local flavours like curried goat and fried conch at one of the seafood shacks. For those looking to stretch their legs, hiking Mount Sage—a 543-metre volcanic peak—offers breathtaking views and a rainforest teeming with wildlife including vocal tree frogs. Anchor in Tortola overnight for a relaxed start to your BVI yacht charter.

stops.heading: Tortola to Norman Island
stops.text: Cruise to Norman Island, famous for its ties to Robert Louis Stevenson’s Treasure Island. Anchor in The Bright, a serene bay perfect for swimming and snorkelling. The adventurous can take the tender to Treasure Point to explore the mysterious sea caves, home to schools of colourful fish. For even more snorkelling, head to Pelican Island and The Indians, where coral gardens teem with marine life. As the sun begins to set, indulge in cocktails at Willy T's—a floating bar known for its lively atmosphere—or dine at Pirates Bight Bar, enjoying a tranquil sunset over the bay.

stops.heading: Norman Island to Peter Island
stops.text: For a day of watersports and relaxation anchor at Little Harbour or Deadman’s Bay, a secluded stretch of soft sand bordered by lush tropical hills. Ashore, visit the Oceans7 Beach Club or indulge in a meal at Deadman’s Bay Beach Bar. For a touch more extravagance, dock at Peter Island Resort in Sprat Bay where world-class wellness and dining facilities await. Their 10,000 sq. ft. spa offers seven luxurious indoor treatment rooms and the resort’s fitness centre is housed in two oceanfront bohios, where you can work out with spectacular views of Big Reef Bay.

stops.heading: Peter Island To Salt, Cooper, And Beef Islands
stops.text: Dive the legendary wreck of the RMS Rhone. Explore the remains of this British mail steamer, which sank in 1867, and swim among the sea life that now calls this historic wreck home. After your dive, cruise to Cooper Island, where you can enjoy lunch at Cooper Island Beach Club, known for its charming atmosphere and local boutiques. Late afternoon, head to your overnight anchorage at Beef Island for cocktails at The Last Resort, a hidden gem set on Bellamy Cay, an islet stranded in the middle of Trellis Bay.

stops.heading: Trellis Bay to Virgin Gorda
stops.text: Cruise to the iconic Baths on Virgin Gorda where giant granite boulders, create spectacle of tidal pools, tunnels, and grottos. Spend the morning wandering through this maze of rocks before hiking to the Top of The Baths restaurant for lunch. In the afternoon, dock at the Bitter End Yacht Club in Gorda Sound, a hub for watersports. Enjoy paddleboarding, windsurfing, or kayaking in the calm waters before a relaxed evening with cocktails on board or ashore at Saba Rock.

stops.heading: Virgin Gorda To Guana Island Or Anegada
stops.text: Cruise to Guana Island, an unspoiled private island that offers complete seclusion. Anchor in White Bay, where you can enjoy a private beach BBQ prepared by your yacht’s chef, or swim in the clear, turquoise waters that surround this pristine location. For a different adventure, weather permitting, head to Anegada—a low-lying coral island famous for its lobster bakes and incredible flats fishing. Here, the island’s uninhabited stretches of beach and local seafood create a sense of true escapism.

stops.heading: Guana Island To Great Camanoe
stops.text: From Guana Island sail to privately owned Great Camanoe. Anchor at Lee Bay, and step ashore to enjoy a private beach picnic prepared by your yacht’s chef, before exploring nearby Cam Bay National Park, where the protected waters host vibrant coral reefs and an array of tropical fish. Birdwatchers will also appreciate the migratory shorebirds that frequent the area. For a more active adventure, hike the island’s nature trails for sweeping views of Scrub Island and Beef Island in the distance. Return to your yacht for sunset cocktails and a special meal under the stars.

stops.heading: Guana Island to Jost Van Dyke
stops.text: Jost Van Dyke, a perennial favourite in the BVI oozes island charm. Anchor in Great Harbour, where beach bars like Foxy’s serve up fresh seafood and rum punch alongside live calypso music. For those seeking adventure, neighbouring Little Jost Van Dyke offers pristine snorkelling and calm waters to explore from the tender. After a day of soaking up the sun, head to the famous Soggy Dollar Bar in White Bay for a signature painkiller cocktail and some island storytelling.

stops.heading: Jost Van Dyke to Tortola
stops.text: After breakfast, enjoy a final swim or paddle board before setting sail for Cane Garden Bay, Tortola’s most famous beach. Known for its lively bars and soft, palm-fringed sands. Drop anchor and spend the day exploring the area—whether relaxing on the beach, enjoying watersports, or taking a tender to Brewers Bay for snorkelling and a scenic hike. For a taste of local culture, visit Callwood Rum Distillery, one of the oldest rum distilleries in the Caribbean, where you can sample the island’s traditional spirits.

stops.heading: Return To Sopers Hole Marina, Tortola
stops.text: After nine days full of exploration return to Soper’s Hole Marina, where you’ll disembark after an unforgettable 10-day journey. Take some time to explore the marina’s local shops or enjoy a waterfront dinner before bidding farewell to your crew and the British Virgin Islands.

caribbean/virgin-islands.title: St Maarten to St Maarten
intro: With a fabulous choice of stunning bays, wonderful marinas and exceptional towns to explore, you will be spoiled for choice during this superyacht charter itinerary.

Cruise calm waters to enjoy an island-hopping adventure in paradise. Whether you seek secluded coves, bustling coastal towns, vibrant nightlife or delicious local cuisine - this itinerary has something for everyone.

stops.heading: simpson bay, st maarten
stops.text: Arrive and be escorted to Marina Isle de Sol, Simpson Bay before sailing to Grande Case to spend the evening at anchor. Before or after your dinner on board, venture ashore for an evening drink. Soak up the French ambiance of a coastal town bustling with cafés and quaint restaurants.

stops.heading: simpson bay to grand case
stops.text: Awake to a full array of yacht toys and enjoy the morning in the bay of Grand Case, where there are no restrictions for waterskiing or jet‐skiing. After lunch on board, your crew will take you to meet a private driver for an afternoon of zip‐lining at Loterie Farm. Then sail the 2 hours to St. Barths for a guided tour of the island, or a leisurely hike up to the old fort to take some photos. Shop in the boutiques or enjoy a day of pampering at one of the magnificent spa’s. Dine at The Eden Roc Hotel before heading to Nikki Beach for drinks.

stops.heading: gustavia
stops.text: After choosing your favourite anchorage in St. Barts and enjoying the warm water, head to the island’s capital, Gustavia, and settle for the night.

stops.heading: st barts to barbuda
stops.text: Head off from St Barths to the island of Barbuda, arriving just in time for lunch. Anchor in Low Bay’s aquamarine waters and explore the endless white sand beaches. After lunch, enjoy a full beach setup with beach games and enjoy the water sports on offer. Enjoy sundowners and sunset views from the jacuzzi on the sundeck.

stops.heading: barbuda to st kitts
stops.text: Sail through the night to St. Kitts and anchor in White House Bay, offering total protection from any weather. Venture ashore or use the water toys available. There is a terrific beach bar at Banana Bay for sundowners.

stops.heading: st kitts
stops.text: Head to shore for a 4x4 off‐road tour, bird tour, railway or rainforest tour. Lunch ashore and then take the tender for an afternoon of offshore fishing. The yacht will then set sail while you sleep, so wake up to a brand new anchorage in Anguilla.

stops.heading: anguilla
stops.text: Awake in Rendezvous Bay, Anguilla. Take advantage of the service of the crew and enjoy beachcombing or hit the beach bars. If there are golfers in your party, this is a great opportunity to play. Anchor in Rendezvous Bay for the night.

stops.heading: st maarten
stops.text: Sail through the night towards St. Maarten, arriving at an anchorage to enjoy the final morning of water sports before returning to dock.

caribbean/virgin-islands.title: St. Thomas to St. Thomas
intro: The U.S. Virgin Islands, a year-round destination, offer some of the finest cruising grounds in the Caribbean, making them firm favourite for superyacht charters.
With calm waters, beautiful beaches, and rich marine life, the region is ideal for both seasoned charterers and newcomers seeking a unique luxury experience.

This seven-day itinerary showcases the finest of the USVI, from the lively ports of St. Thomas to the pristine, protected bays of St. John, blending adventure with relaxation. You’ll find endless opportunities for snorkelling, diving, and hiking, all within the serenity and privacy of the islands’ sheltered anchorages. Every day brings a new discovery, whether it’s exploring untouched coral reefs or enjoying a beachside meal at a local restaurant. For those seeking a balance of luxury, nature, and adventure, this Caribbean itinerary offers a perfect blend.

stops.heading: St. Thomas to Magens Bay
stops.text: Begin your adventure at Yacht Haven Grande Marina in St. Thomas. After boarding your yacht, cruise to one of the Caribbean’s most picturesque beaches, Magens Bay. Named one of the Top 10 Best Beaches by USA Today, and featured in famous films like The Twilight Saga, Magens Bay is a must visit. Enjoy watersports and stroll along the expansive stretch of soft sand or enjoy a refreshing swim in the clear, shallow waters. As the day winds down, relax on deck while your personal chef prepares some local flavours such as curried goat, fried conch or johnny cakes with views of the lush hills surrounding the bay as your backdrop. This beautiful setting will be your peaceful home for the night.

stops.heading: Magens Bay to Botany Bay
stops.text: After a morning swim in Magens Bay, cruise along St. Thomas's scenic north coast to Botany Bay, a pristine and secluded spot on the island's western tip. Anchor near Sandy Bay Beach, an idyllic setting for a private beach setup and barbecue. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon with freshly prepared local dishes like grilled lobster or jerk chicken. For a touch of adventure, take a short hike to Mermaid’s Chair, where the Atlantic meets the Caribbean in a unique strip of sand. Relax on deck as the sun sets over this quiet haven, soaking in the tranquil beauty before an overnight stay in this serene anchorage.

stops.heading: Botany Bay to Francis Bay, St. John (via Lovango and Congo Cut)
stops.text: A leisurely cruise to Lovango and Congo Cut will present opportunities for daytime hiking and a decadent lunch at Lovango Beach Club. After lunch head to your overnight anchorage at Francis Bay. Located within the U.S. Virgin Islands National Park, this spot is famous for its pristine beaches and abundant sea turtles. Spend late afternoon snorkelling, swimming, or relaxing on deck, and if you’re up for an adventure, take an early morning hike with spectacular views of the island. The peaceful surroundings and natural beauty make this the perfect anchorage for the night.

stops.heading: Francis Bay to Cruz Bay and Waterlemon Cay
stops.text: Cruise to Waterlemon Cay, where you’ll take the tender ashore to Cruz Bay, St. John’s main port and vibrant social hub. Here, enjoy a leisurely afternoon exploring chic boutiques and local shops before returning to Waterlemon Cay, one of the premier snorkelling sites in the U.S. Virgin Islands. The calm, shallow waters around the cay are perfect for snorkellers of all levels, revealing a lively marine world filled with sea turtles, rays, and colourful reef fish. For a dose of history, a short hike from the beach leads to the ruins of an 18th-century Danish plantation, adding a fascinating cultural dimension to this idyllic spot. End your day unwinding on board, surrounded by the beauty of this natural haven.

stops.heading: Waterlemon Cay to Coral Bay
stops.text: Cruise to Round Bay, a gem on the St John's quiet east coast. The bay is perfect for water sports, from paddleboarding to kayaking, or simply enjoying the serenity of this lesser-known anchorage. Take the tender to explore nearby Coral Bay, a laid-back, local town with a charming blend of casual beach bars, small boutiques, and art galleries. A short cruise will bring you to Hurricane Hole, a protected area within the Virgin Islands Coral Reef National Monument. Known for its rich biodiversity, the mangrove-lined shorelines of Hurricane Hole offer incredible snorkelling, with hidden nurseries for juvenile fish and marine creatures.

stops.heading: Coral Bay to Reef Bay
stops.text: Departing Coral Bay, set a course for Reef Bay, a secluded haven on St. John's southern coast. Upon arrival, anchor near the historic Reef Bay Sugar Mill Ruins, a testament to the island's 19th-century sugar production era. Accessible via a short hike from the beach, these well-preserved ruins offer a glimpse into the island's colonial past. For snorkelling enthusiasts, the nearby waters around Ditleff Point present vibrant coral formations and diverse marine life, providing an underwater adventure in a tranquil setting. As evening approaches, enjoy the serene ambiance of Reef Bay, surrounded by lush hills and the gentle sounds of the Caribbean Sea, making it an ideal spot for a spectacular dinner on board and a peaceful overnight anchorage.

stops.heading: Reef Bay to Honeymoon Beach and Disembark at Charlotte Amalie
stops.text: After a relaxing breakfast, set off for Honeymoon Beach, a picture-perfect cove known for its pristine sands and gentle, turquoise waters. Spend the morning soaking up the sun, swimming, or taking a scenic hike along the Lind Point Trail, where tropical foliage and coastal views create an idyllic backdrop for a final island adventure. After lunch, cruise back to St. Thomas, arriving at Charlotte Amalie by midday. Here, take in the vibrant sights of the island’s bustling town, with time for some last-minute shopping or a leisurely waterfront lunch. Conclude your unforgettable journey at Yacht Haven Grande Marina, where your crew will bid you a warm farewell.

central-america/costa-rica.title: panama to costa rica
intro: This luxurious Panamá - Costa Rica itinerary promises a sensory feast across two vibrant countries. As part of your Panama yacht charter, expect a heady mix of tropical jungles and wildlife-rich national parks, not to mention glorious palm-fringed beaches that span across Panama to Costa Rica.

Explore beautiful beaches, dense rainforests and meet indigenous wildlife on this fabulous Panama Costa Rica itinerary. Cruising to lush islands, there is the opportunity to be as active or relaxed as you wish. Make the most of the warm, calm seas and enjoy the onboard watertoys inventory to the max. Experience Central America like never before as you seamlessly journey between two countries by sea, uncovering the secrets of each destination, living the adventure every step of the way.

stops.heading: panama city
stops.text: Embark in Flamenco Marina, Panama City and settle on board. Enjoy a visit to the Gatun Lake and explore Fort San Lorenzo. Another interesting site here is the Panama Canal Expansion Observation Centre. Returning to Panama City, it is fascinating watching the ships navigating the locks and the Canal Museum nearby is an interesting drop-in.
