Venture to the heart of Panama City, experiencing the buzz of its lively markets and the rich culture that permeates every street corner. Perhaps take an evening walking tour through the lovely Casco Viejo (old Panama City) and spend the first night in port.

stops.heading: panama city to pearl islands
stops.text: Leave early morning and cruise to the Pearl Islands. Enjoy swimming and snorkelling in the clear, warm waters. Later sail to Punta Patino, the largest nature reserve in Central America. This is where you may spot Panama's national bird, the Harpy Eagle. Owned by ANCON, a private conservation group, the wildlife here is astounding. Experience the tranquillity of this protected area as the sun sets, the sounds of nature providing a harmonious soundtrack to the end of your day.

stops.heading: mogue embera reserve
stops.text: The yacht can arrange an excursion to the Mogue Embera Reserve, where you will paddle upstream in dugout canoes to reach Mogue village, passing through the mesmerising mangroves ecosystem. One of the seven indigenous groups living in Panama, the Embera Indians, call this home. Very friendly and welcoming, they are known for their time-honoured traditions and beautiful handicrafts. Capture unique memories as you immerse yourself in the rich Embera culture, learning about their way of life, history, and their deep connection to nature.

stops.heading: restingue island
stops.text: Cruise to Caleta Caiman, Restingue Island for a morning of fabulous snorkelling and swimming in total paradise. For lunch head to the nearby tropical beauty of Cebaco Island for a beach BBQ. Take time to enjoy the lovely sandy beach and warm seas. Treat yourself to an afternoon nap under the shade of towering palm trees, or get your heart racing with some exciting watersports. Sail to Golfo Dulce for overnight anchorage.

stops.heading: casa orquideas
stops.text: Sail through Golfito (clear immigration) and continue to nearby Casa Orquideas Private Reserve. This beautiful flower sanctuary is wonderful to wander around and view the extensive grounds. Inhale the fragrant air, filled with the scent of exotic flowers, and marvel at the vibrant bursts of colour that dot the landscape. Head across the bay to Puerto Jiminez for an evening of relaxation.

stops.heading: puerto jimenez
stops.text: Take a leisurely early morning cruise to Puerto Jimenez and anchor off the Oso Peninsula. This park is one of the biological corridors that leads to the amazing Corcovado National Park. Walk through the forests and enjoy up-close interaction with native wildlife. Relax on board and use the watersports equipment for some leisure time later in the day. Feel the rush of adrenaline as you embark on a thrilling zip-line adventure through the verdant rainforest canopy, observing the diverse ecosystem from a bird's-eye view. Spend overnight at anchor near Quepos.

stops.heading: quepos
stops.text: Head ashore in Quepos where you can visit the ruggedly beautiful Manuel Antonio Reserve. Renowned for vast biodiversity of flora and fauna, there are meandering hiking trails from coast to mountain and some fabulous white sand beaches that are a huge draw. Spot lazy sloths hanging in the trees and listen to the chatter of monkeys as you embark on a guided jungle tour. Should you feel adventurous, take the forest canopy or Savegre River excursion for a thrilling activity.

stops.heading: playa bisanz to puerto caldera
stops.text: Enjoy a relaxed last morning at Playa Bisanz for some swimming, snorkelling and watersports fun. Sail to Puerto Caldera for disembarking. As you sail towards the horizon, reflect on the incredible journey you've embarked on during your unforgettable Panama to Costa Rica luxury yacht charter.

central-america/costa-rica.teaser: This luxurious Panamá - Costa Rica itinerary promises a sensory feast across two vibrant countries. Expect a heady mix of tropical jungles and wildlife-rich national parks.

central-america/mexico.title: la paz to la paz
intro: The narrow Sea of Cortez is flanked by mainland Mexico and Baja California, offering an intriguing coastline that remains somewhat of a secret destination.

Aptly named “the world’s aquarium” by Jacques Cousteau, the waters here, on your La Paz yacht charter, thrive with an abundance of fascinating marine mammals such as whale sharks, humpbacks, sea lions and mobula rays.

The contrasting, rugged desert islands are scattered across the sea, rising with towering cacti-dotted crags, while powder-sand beaches are strewn below. These hidden gems are ideally discovered by yacht, making sailing La Paz a unique experience to explore and appreciate the wealth of natural treasures on offer.

stops.heading: la paz to balandra cove
stops.text: Once settled on board, the La Paz yacht charter will get underway, and head to an anchorage in the stunning bay at Balandra Cove. Keep your eyes out for pods of dolphins playing in the warm water along the route. During the afternoon take time to enjoy the water toys in the crystal-clear, shallow water and then take a sunset cruise around the gorgeous Baja California bay on the yachts’ tender. Look out for the El Hongo de Balandra (translated at the mushroom of Balandra) – a unique rock structure resulting from thousands of years of erosion. Star gazing at night will soon become your favourite pastime.

stops.heading: balandra cove to isla espiritu santo
stops.text: Watch the undulating scenery unfold as you are sailing La Paz to Bahia San Gabriel at the southern end of uninhabited Isla Espiritu Santo. Renowned for a geological rainbow of colours, the vibrant red, pink and brown volcanic rocks lapped by bright aquamarine sea and fringed by white sands are an incredible sight. Punta Prieta to the north end offers sublime snorkelling grounds, while hikers will enjoy the trail leading from the beach to beautiful Playa Bonanza on the east side. A declared UNESCO Natural Protected Area and World Heritage Site, the biodiversity of endemic flora and fauna, varied marine life together with important archaeological remains found here is astounding. Take time to explore on the tender, kayaks or wave runners and head ashore to stroll along white-sand beaches plus some amazing snorkelling.

stops.heading: espiritu santo to isla partida
stops.text: Separated by a narrow channel next to Espiritu Santo island, experience the beauty of enchanting Isla Partida at sunrise, a standout location during your La Paz sailing journey. and drop anchor in the turquoise waters on the northern tip at Ensenada Grande. Watch lively sea lions frolicking in the waters at the nearby Los Islotes islands whilst taking a leisurely breakfast on the flybridge. Tender over to explore and take the unique opportunity to swim with the sea lion pups as they playfully whirl around you – a truly memorable experience. Go to the eastern side of Isla Partida for some lively snorkelling spots and marvel at the reefs twinkling with life in the sunshine. On land visit the sea caves and explore the beaches famed for turtle nests. Great fishing action can be found at Marisla Seamount a few miles away, which is also a top spot for diving with manta rays and schools of hammerhead sharks.

stops.heading: isla partida to isla san francisco
stops.text: On your La Paz yacht charter, cruise to anchor in Half Moon Bay at uninhabited Isla San Francisco, once homeland to gold miners and pearl prospectors. Soak up the relaxed atmosphere amongst complete tranquillity and snorkel the rocky reefs with yellow-tail surgeonfish. Enjoy the yachts’ tenders and toys for a day of fun, soak up the sun on deck and try paddle boarding in the secluded bay. For those seeking adventure, hike to the top of the mountain for a stunning panoramic view and watch for schools of bottlenose dolphins leaping out of the water. Nearby inhabited Isla Coyote, aside from a wealth of snorkelling sites, offers a great place to mix with the friendly local fishermen – go to the quaint cantina perched on top of the hill for a warm welcome. The village itself is charming with a whale museum and some interesting sculptures. Alternatively explore Bahia Amortajada - through the dense mangroves you will find a beautiful lagoon to snorkel or kayak along the reef - also a perfect spot to admire the flocks of pelicans splashing around. Walk along the white sandy shoreline flanked by cactus gardens, red mountains and turquoise waters.

stops.heading: isla san francisco to isla carmen
stops.text: As part of your yacht charter in La Paz, cruise across the calm Sea of Cortez early and enjoy breakfast whilst passing through the Loreto Triangle; you will see Bahia Balandra in the distance. The yacht will drop hook in a protected anchorage ready for guests to enjoy a full day of activities. Set in the Loreto Bay Marine Park, Isla Carmen is one of the largest islands. Tender ashore to explore this once bustling salt mining community, now turned to ghost town, with a mile-long pink salt pond. Birdwatching enthusiasts will delight in the species here, such as the scissor-tailed flycatcher, brown pelican and blue-footed booby, together with abundant nesting sites for local seabirds. Equally, the water flourishes with marine life including turtles, orcas, dolphins and sea lions, a veritable nirvana for snorkellers and divers. From the yacht, soak up views in undisturbed tranquillity over the Gulf of California and the looming Sierra del Gigante on the mainland above Loreto.

stops.heading: isla carmen to isla monserrate
stops.text: Start the journey back south on your La Paz yacht charter, with the yacht anchoring off the deserted island of Monserrate. Very few visitors stop here, so you can relish the complete privacy and isolation. The clear waters are teeming with fish and it is an ideal location to try reef fishing or billfishing – today’s catch can be tonight’s dinner! Enjoy time snorkelling around the craggy cliffs with friendly manta rays and whale sharks. Yellowstone beach on the north end, named for the mustard colour of the sandstone cliffs, is almost a mile of pristine sand and a lovely place for a relaxed stroll and snorkelling. Diving at Isla Galeras, a small set of islets about 2 miles north, is superb – expect rocky ledges populated by large schools of yellowtail snappers and pacific creol fish – guitar sharks are often spotted here too.

stops.heading: isla monserrate to isla pardita
stops.text: Enjoy the final full day of your yacht charter La Paz in an anchorage at the Partida Cove. Packed with secret spots to explore on waverunners or kayaks - at high tide take a dinghy ride through the channel between Partida and Espiritu Santo to explore the fascinating sea caves. Alternatively, at low tide, the sandbar pass is a unique place to enjoy a picnic and some fun beach games. Some 6 miles north of Partida is the El Bajo seamount and an ideal dive site. This group of pinnacles hidden some 60 feet below the water is very popular with moray eels, mantas, whale sharks and hammerheads. After a day of activity on the beach and in the water, spend the evening relaxing on deck with a mouth-watering dinner prepared by your dedicated chef.

stops.heading: isla pardita to la paz
stops.text: End your memorable sailing La Paz adventure as the Captain gets the yacht underway during brunch on board, passing by Espiritu Santo on the way through the Bahia de la Paz. Once ashore enjoy the small seaside city of La Paz with its wonderful waterfront malecon walkway and local markets. Stop at a seaside cantina to enjoy a locally made margarita and a fish taco as a perfect end to your voyage of island discovery.

central-america/mexico.teaser: The narrow Sea of Cortez is flanked by mainland Mexico and Baja California, offering an intriguing coastline that still remains somewhat of a secret destination.

indian-ocean/maldives.title: Male to Male
intro: With irresistible white beaches and deep blue lagoons, island hopping in the Maldives is a getaway in paradise. Idyllic scenery, tasty cuisine and exceptional marine life make this a true dream destination for an exceptional yacht charter experience.

Few of the 100 islets are inhabited, however, all are blessed with stunning sandy bays and verdant landscapes. Unless you crave a longer cruise, your charter won’t have to leave the North or South Male Atolls to show you the countless delights of the Seychelles. Besides, short cruising distances leave more time to savour the pristine beaches, the warm water and the flawless climate. From December to May, high cruising season, the weather is mild and dry.

stops.heading: male
stops.text: Embark your yacht in Male, capital of the Maldives, with direct flights from Europe, Asia and the Middle East. A massage can be pre-booked for you at the upscale spa in the One & Only Reethi Rah resort, to ease away any jet lag. should you wish.

stops.heading: hembadhu
stops.text: The islet of Hembadhu has superb dive and snorkeling sites, with more than 600 species of exotic fish and even a shipwreck on a reef that’s easily accessible for everyone to explore.

stops.heading: huvafen
stops.text: An enclosed lagoon, Huvafen is a wonderland for naturalists both above and below the water. The star attraction here is the world’s first underwater spa: pamper yourselves with a treatment in a double room while gazing at the fish swimming among coral reefs

stops.heading: maadhu finolhu
stops.text: Head on to this deserted paradise surrounded by a vast lagoon that acts as an aquarium filled with brightly colored fish. Ask the chef for a bag of bread scraps and make a thousand fish happy.

stops.heading: makunufshi
stops.text: Cruise over to South Male Atoll and explore Makunufushi, where you can choose between a dive on Kandooma Channel (one of the best wall-diving sites in the Maldives) or snorkeling along a quiet reef nearby. Dine on deck under a gazillion stars with a gentle trade wind blowing.

stops.heading: emboodhu finolhu
stops.text: This island features one of the largest lagoons in the Maldives—with the Taj Exotica resort right in the middle of it. Break out the yacht’s water toys for a day of play

stops.heading: male
stops.text: Return to Male and take time to visit the exotic minaret, explore the street market or browse the shops for local art and crafts before returning to the ordinary world.

indian-ocean/maldives.teaser: With irresistible white beaches and deep blue lagoons, island-hopping in the Maldives is sheer paradise. In this tropical haven enjoy idyllic scenery, tasty cuisine and exceptional marine life.

indian-ocean/seychelles.title: Eden Island to Fregate Island, Seychelles
intro: Offering a unique experience of untapped tropical scenery, flavours and scents, the perfect weather and relaxed atmosphere of the Seychelles provides an idyllic charter getaway.

The Seychelles are simply spectacular, with palms arching gracefully above clear lagoons, coral reefs ready for snorkelers and divers, tropical scenery and mild weather with endless sunshine. Each of the isles could be labelled “the classic desert island,” and you will feel like Robinson Crusoe when you see them.

Few of the 100 islets are inhabited, however, all are blessed with stunning sandy bays and verdant landscapes. Unless you crave a longer cruise, your charter won’t have to leave the North or South Male Atolls to show you the countless delights of the Seychelles. Besides, short cruising distances leave more time to savour the pristine beaches, the warm water and the flawless climate. From December to May, high cruising season, the weather is mild and dry.
The Seychelles can be whatever you want them to be, from beachcombing a deserted shoreline, to snorkelling a spectacular reef, to enjoying exceptional restaurant cuisine - and so much more.

stops.heading: eden island
stops.text: Arrive at Victoria International Airport and transfer directly to the yacht. You can board either in the beautiful marina of Eden Island or take a tender transfer out to anchor. Either way the airport is just a 10 minute drive from the vessel and the beautiful mountainous backdrop will leave you awe inspired from the moment you land. Take time to wander around some of the superb shops within the marina or perhaps spend the first day at anchor in Saint Anne Marine National Park enjoying the water sports equipment.

stops.heading: beau vallon beach
stops.text: Take a leisurely one hour cruise to Beau Vallon Beach, a favourite spot for local families thanks to the shallow, clear waters, ideal for snorkelling. The scenery is breath-taking, with pristine sands and swaying palms set against a rich backdrop of lush mountains. Visitors can enjoy a good selection of excellent restaurants and shops next to the beach, as well as a weekly night market just a 20 minute drive from the main town of Victoria.

stops.heading: cap ternay marine park
stops.text: Another short cruise takes the yacht around to Cap Ternay Marine Park to anchor in a secluded spot off a picturesque beach where a freshwater stream runs to the sea. This protected marine park is achingly beautiful, with warm, clear water offering a myriad of diving and snorkelling opportunities in the reefs on either side of the bay. Look out for eagle rays as you explore the vibrant marine life below the surface. Relax on the idyllic beach with panoramic views over to Morne Seychellois peak, the island’s tallest mountain.

stops.heading: petite anse
stops.text: At Petit Anse, the award winning Four Seasons Hotel and Beach is nestled in the beautiful bay, surrounded by stunning scenery. Discover a host of excellent restaurants plus spa treatments that can be enjoyed either in resort or brought on board to maximise tranquil relaxation. On the beach the ribbons of soft sand flanked by weather-worn boulders provide a naturally beautiful setting. This tropical paradise is renowned for a truly relaxed atmosphere, so take the opportunity to unwind in paradise by swimming and snorkelling at leisure.

stops.heading: anse lazio
stops.text: After cruising for approximately three hours in the early morning, you will arrive at Anse Lazio, on the northwest of Praslin Island, just in time to enjoy a leisurely breakfast on the sun deck. Possibly one of the best kept secrets in the Seychelles, soak up the sensational views as azure waves lap the powder white shores. Here is a great place to plan an action packed day using all the water sports and snorkel amongst the coral whilst looking out for turtles.

stops.heading: curieuse island
stops.text: Take a short hop over to Curieuse island, where there are stunning anchorages. This small granite island is noted for its bare red earth strewn with the unique coco de mer palms, one of the Seychelles cultural icons and only found on two neighbouring islands. This is the natural habitat of the highly entertaining, wild, giant tortoises who will come to greet you and enjoy being hand fed. Walk from one side of the island to the other, through mangroves teeming with wildlife and discover tiny deserted coves dotted around the coastline.

stops.heading: la digue island
stops.text: La Digue is blessed with stunning natural beauty where granite rocks, turquoise water, tranquil bays and vibrant coral reefs make up this yachting haven. There are local guides if you wish to organise hiking and rock-climbing tours or sign up for surfing lessons, as it is an idyllic spot to learn. Climb to the top of the island for panoramic views whilst learning about the amazing indigenous flora and fauna.

stops.heading: Felicite Island
stops.text: The amazing resort island of Felicité is a wonderful location for another action packed day of watersports. This lush, granite isle is just a short tender ride from one of the best snorkelling spots in the world where the abundant marine life is fascinating. The luxurious Six Senses private island resort is an idyllic ecological sanctuary, where relaxation is key. From exquisite dining to spa treatments, this is a great spot to indulge in perfect relaxation on powder-white sands.

stops.heading: fregate island
stops.text: Cruise for three hours overnight to spend the last day experiencing the charm of Anse Victorin on the private island resort of Fregate Island. Although small, this beach is simply perfect and no wonder it has been awarded the title of most beautiful beach in the world multiple times. From here surfing with onboard instructors, a last dive or even catching that last tuna is the goal. Take a leisurely four hour cruise back to the main island of Mahé, which can be timed for departure, or enjoy a day back in Saint Anne Marine nature park before heading home.

indian-ocean/seychelles.teaser: Offering a unique experience of untapped tropical scenery, flavours and scents, the perfect weather and relaxed atmosphere of the Seychelles provides an idyllic charter getaway.

mediterranean/croatia.title: Dubrovnik to Trogir
intro: Explore gorgeous backdrops and exciting sailing along the coastline of Croatia. The stunning beaches, secluded coves and traditional villages are all best accessed by superyacht.

From Dubrovnik to Trogir, take in some of the stunning shorelines in Croatia. From the green expanse of relaxed Mljet to the bustle of historic Hvar, there are countless towns, beaches and national parks for charterers to enjoy.

stops.heading: dubrovnik
stops.text: The best known sailing destination in Croatia, Dubrovnik is a beautifully preserved city with a distinctive Old Town encircled by massive stone walls. The well-preserved buildings range from Baroque St. Blaise Church to Renaissance Sponza Palace and Gothic Rector’s Palace. Anchor and explore the cultural attractions.

stops.heading: mljet
stops.text: The beautiful island of Mljet, with its relaxed Mediterranean atmosphere, is a perfect first stop on your cruise. The Croatian Islands are renowned for scenic saltwater lakes and pristine waters. Try out your yacht’s water toys.

stops.heading: vis
stops.text: Vis is a superlative island with a stunning blue grotto, peaceful, deserted beaches, vineyard blanketed hills and olive groves. Go ashore for a walk through the dense greenery.

stops.heading: hvar
stops.text: Don’t miss the chance to visit Hvar, well known for its welcoming locals as well as its myriad historical and cultural sights. Effusive in the summer, peaceful and idyllic in the winter, Hvar is a fantastic island always erring on the side of sophistication.

stops.heading: brac
stops.text: Enjoy Croatia’s most popular beach, Bol, on the coast of Brac. Here you can relax, sunbathe and enjoy the water sports from snorkelling to windsurfing.

stops.heading: split
stops.text: Anchor in the welcoming seaport of Split with its picturesque old town. Explore the emperor Diocletian’s palace and wander through the cosmopolitan streets enjoying the fine dining and dynamic energy as the town comes into its own at night.

stops.heading: trogir
stops.text: The final stop, Trogir, is an ideal place to end your charter. Watch the sunset while sipping cocktails at one of the many romantic bars along the coastline.

mediterranean/croatia.teaser: Explore gorgeous backdrops and exciting sailing along the coastline of Croatia. The stunning beaches, secluded coves and traditional villages are all best accessed by superyacht.

mediterranean/croatia.title: Split to Dubrovnik
intro: Seven days on the Dalmatian coast moves through some of the most varied sailing in the Adriatic: a UNESCO-listed Roman palace, an island that spent four decades as a closed military zone, pine forests reaching the water's edge, and the medieval walls of Dubrovnik at the end of it.

This Croatia yacht charter itinerary runs Split to Dubrovnik via Maslinica, Vis, Hvar, Korčula, Mljet and Šipan, covering the central and southern Dalmatian coast at a pace that leaves time to actually be in each place.

Croatia has over 1,200 islands along its Adriatic coastline. Most charter guests never need more than a dozen of them. There are plenty of reasons to charter in Croatia beyond this single route, but the itinerary below covers the best of the central and south Dalmatian islands in seven days, with a clearly optional extension into Montenegro for those who want more.

stops.heading: Split and Maslinica
stops.text: Embarkation is in Split. The morning before embarkation goes to Diocletian’s Palace, a Roman emperor’s retirement complex built in the fourth century and now the living heart of Split’s Old Town, with restaurants, bars and apartments occupying the original imperial apartments and mausoleum. It’s one of the better-preserved Roman structures in Europe and worth the hour ashore before the yacht slips its lines. The cruise to Maslinica takes around an hour. Sitting on the western tip of Šolta island, Maslinica is one of the most sheltered anchorages in central Dalmatia: a small harbour village overlooked by the eighteenth-century Martinis Marchi castle on its own islet at the bay’s entrance, with olive groves running back into the hills behind. The waterfront has a handful of excellent restaurants, and the pace is noticeably slower than Split. Dinner ashore or on board, with a walk out to the castle islet for those who want the view back over the bay at sunset.

stops.heading: Maslinica to Vis
stops.text: The morning is unhurried, with time to explore Maslinica’s waterfront and, tide and appetite allowing, a swim in one of the coves nearby before the yacht heads for Vis. Vis is the furthest inhabited island from the Croatian mainland, and the quietest stop on the route. It was closed to all foreign visitors from the late 1940s until 1989, used as a major Yugoslav naval base with over 20 kilometres of underground tunnels carved into the island’s interior. That isolation preserved it. The fishing villages, the food, the landscape and the pace of life on Vis feel noticeably different from the islands that have had decades of tourism to contend with. Stern to in Vis town for a fascinating tour of the underground tunnels with a local guide, before heading south. Enjoy an afternoon tender ride around the coast before the yacht docks in Komiža Bay on the southwest side of the island, a small fishing village with a harbour full of traditional wooden boats. Komiža has some excellent lobster restaurants, perfect for a dinner ashore.

stops.heading: The Pakleni Islands and Hvar
stops.text: Komiža gets one last unhurried look before the yacht heads for Hvar, with the afternoon spent at anchor in the Pakleni Islands, the scatter of pine-covered islets just off Hvar that offer some of the best swimming and watersports on the route. Lunch on board, tenders in the water. The tender ride into Hvar Town in the afternoon takes minutes. Hvar has a reputation for nightlife and beach clubs, and the main square delivers on both if that is what the group wants. It is also genuinely beautiful, and the views from the old fortress above the town over the Pakleni Islands and out to the open Adriatic are worth the climb alone. Anchor overnight in the islands or in the harbour.

stops.heading: Hvar to Korčula
stops.text: The morning belongs to Hvar before the yacht moves on. Korčula is described as Little Dubrovnik for its medieval stone architecture, its walls and towers and the density of its old town crammed onto a small peninsula. It’s also claimed, with varying levels of evidence, as the birthplace of Marco Polo. The old town is worth an evening: dinner ashore in one of the restaurants in the old walls, with the Adriatic on three sides. The passage takes between 3-4 hours, depending on conditions. The yacht anchors for lunch at a bay on the way across, chosen on the day.

stops.heading: Korčula to Mljet National Park
stops.text: Mljet is the green island, and one of Croatia’s truly beautiful national parks. Dense pine and oak forests run to the water’s edge, and the national park in the western third of the island contains two saltwater lakes connected by a channel, Malo Jezero and Veliko Jezero, surrounded by woodland with a small Benedictine monastery sitting on an island in the larger lake. The yacht stern-ties among the trees, lunch on board, and the afternoon is on foot: a walk through the pine forest to Veliko Jezero, a boat trip to the monastery, a swim in the lake. Dinner on board as the light drops into the forest. The passage from Korčula takes around two hours. Mljet National Park requires an entry fee, paid on arrival.

stops.heading: Mljet to Šipan
stops.text: A last morning in Mljet National Park before the yacht heads for the Elaphiti Islands, the small archipelago scattered southwest of Dubrovnik. Šipan is the largest of the group and the quietest: no cars, no crowds, just olive groves, old stone farmhouses, and a scatter of ruined summer villas built by Dubrovnik’s nobility, who used the island as a retreat from the city for centuries. The yacht ties up in Šipanska Luka, the main village on the island’s southwestern coast, where a scatter of restaurants line the small harbour. The afternoon is unhurried: a walk up through the olive terraces, a swim off the yacht, or simply time on deck watching the light change over the bay. Dinner ashore at one of the harbourside restaurants, or on board if the group prefers to stay put.

stops.heading: Šipan to Dubrovnik: Disembark
stops.text: The final passage is short, around an hour and a half, and brings the yacht into Dubrovnik itself. The tender ride into the Old Town takes only minutes from the anchorage: the medieval walls, the Stradun, the Rector’s Palace and the cable car to the top of Mount Srđ for the view over the walled city and the Adriatic beyond. Final breakfast on board, with time for a last look at Dubrovnik’s Old Town before disembarkation. Or, for those who want to continue, the optional Montenegro extension begins here.

stops.heading: Optional Extension: Montenegro
stops.text: Guests wishing to extend into Montenegro should note that departing Croatian waters at Dubrovnik requires a formal customs clearance. This isn’t a complex process but it needs to be planned in advance with the Captain. It isn’t a simple continuation of the same cruise. The passage from Dubrovnik to Kotor takes between 2-3 hours. Kotor sits deep into the Bay of Kotor, a deep fjord-like inlet in the Montenegrin coast, with a walled old town and mountains rising steeply behind it. Day 8 continues to Portonovi, with the Aman resort available for dinner or a spa visit. Day 9 runs the Montenegro coast to Budva or directly to Tivat for departure, depending on the group’s schedule.

mediterranean/france.title: Cannes to Monaco
intro: Enjoy cruising the glittering French coastline. Explore market towns, admire architecture, enjoy fine cuisine and soak up the beautiful scenery.

Nowhere else in the world has the concentration of wealth, sophistication and cultural finesse as the Côte d’Azur. Often referred to as the Millionaire’s Mediterranean Playground, here you can put on the glitz, experience the cachet of casinos, visit galleries and taste some of the finest food in the world. Then drop anchor, sip some chilled rosé and watch the sun set over a picturesque mountainous backdrop. Small wonder it’s the place to be seen.

stops.heading: cannes
stops.text: Cannes is the glamorous beating heart of the Cote d’Azur. Natural harbour-side beauty sits sympathetically beside brazen opulence in this highly desirable place to see and be seen. In the sunshine, couture shops and art deco hotels of La Croisette impress with the chic glamour of days gone by. Ferraris and Porsches cruise the strip and celebrity-spotting is easy along striped-lounger private beaches. The palmshaded promenade affords an easy walk whilst revealing open views of the Baie de Cannes and nearby Estérel mountains. Legendary, multi-starred hotels such as the Martinez and the Carlton, renowned for historical visits from an abundance of stars over the years, set a benchmark in exclusive privacy

stops.heading: the lerin islands
stops.text: The Lerins are a group of four tiny islands a short hop from Cannes, well worth visiting to while away the hours. The two main islands are Sainte- Marguerite and Saint-Honorat; the micro islands are Tradelière and St-Féréol. Drop anchor in Plateau du Mileu, the shallow, protected passage between the two main islands and visit the nearest and largest: luscious Ile Sainte Marguerite is smothered in a carpet of fragrant Allepo pine and eucalyptus with wide pathways artistically criss-crossing the island. Bring nets and snorkelling gear - bursting with tiny rocky bays it’s a great place for rockpooling and crabbing with younger travellers, with just one long sandy beach in this haven of calm with no traffic.

stops.heading: antibes
stops.text: The thriving superyacht port of Antibes, encircled by ancient stone walls, exudes a relaxed beachy feel backed by a gorgeous old town with narrow cobbled streets, markets and thriving café culture. If you want to combine great beaches, culture, history and good food, Antibes will match your needs. Traditional and bustling, Port Vauban is the largest marina in Europe, where a selection of the biggest and most glamorous yachts afloat anchor during the summer months. The old town is a warren of quaint cafes, bars and boutiques with a busy Provençal market where wafts of fragrant lavender mixed with ripe local cheeses drift in the air.

stops.heading: nice
stops.text: A globally renowned tourist destination, Nice epitomises the French Mediterranean with seashores, mountains and architecture all with equal appeal. Bustling with life, stroll the streets to enjoy infectious cafe culture whilst taking time to admire the Belle Epoque architecture and Baroque houses.

stops.heading: st jean cap ferrat
stops.text: Providing a great anchorage, St Jean Cap Ferrat, near Villefranche, is a ragged headland where substantial private homes are just visible from the water. Enjoying a position in the centre of the French Riviera, between Monaco and Nice, Cap Ferrat is notable for its clutch of exclusive hotels, restaurants and beach clubs, and ideally placed for quick access to many destinations all along the Cote d’Azur. Long, languid days can be spent swimming off the back deck, diving in the incredible waters and snoozing on the beaches – themselves a catwalk of beauty and glamour.

stops.heading: eze
stops.text: The perched village of Eze, with it's clusters of houses atop rocky cliffs, commands incredible views. One of the most celebrated French Riviera resorts, situated at an altitude of 426m above sea level, the old village is a maze of narrow, winding streets and shady squares. At the very top the ruined castle of Eza boasts stunning botanical gardens set on the steep slopes - simply perfect to wander and soak up the views.

stops.heading: monaco
stops.text: The principality of Monaco is the world’s second smallest country, making up for its size with immense personality. Sitting atop a narrow coastal area with three sides bounded by France and facing the dazzling Mediterranean, it is an inexcusably thrilling destination. One of the most beautiful harbours set against dramatic cliffs and brimming with mega-yachts exudes an aura of exclusive elegance. High-end shopping, luxurious hotels and five casinos are all skilfully condensed into an area just 1.25 square miles to top off the intoxicating allure of Monaco.

mediterranean/france.teaser: Enjoy cruising the glittering French coastline. Explore quaint perched towns, admire Baroque architecture, enjoy fine cuisine and soak up the beautiful scenery.

mediterranean/france.title: monaco to rome
intro: The Italian coastline is a wonderful yacht charter destination, filled with diversity and something special to please all tastes. Whether seeking a romantic getaway, a multi-generational family holiday or time with good friends, there is magic to be found on your Monaco to Rome yacht itinerary.

From glittering Monaco to the charms of chic Portofino, the colourful appeal of Cinque Terre to the beauty of Elba, cruising these endless coastal delights on board a luxury yacht is an exhilarating journey from Monaco to Italy. The Italian Riviera, a stunning stretch from Monaco to Rome, is renowned for its mild climate, prolific heritage sites and classical atmosphere; the perfect destination to experience an unforgettable luxury yacht charter.

stops.heading: monaco
stops.text: Embark your yacht in the glittering port of Monaco. The principality of Monaco is the world’s second smallest country, making up for its size with immense personality. Sitting atop narrow coastal area with three sides bounded by France and facing the dazzling Mediterranean, it is an inexcusably thrilling destination. As your Monaco to Rome yacht charter sets sail, marvel at one of the most beautiful harbours set against dramatic cliffs and brimming with mega yachts, exuding an aura of exclusive elegance.

stops.heading: portofino
stops.text: Vibrant and charming, Portofino is a splash of colourful houses sat against a riot of lush hillside greenery and sapphire blue waters. Renowned for emanating style, the beating heart is the piazzetta, nestling in a small coastal nook, teeming with chic bars, boutiques and restaurants. Luxury yachts bob in the sparkling bay and anchorages abound. Enjoy a leisurely stroll, refresh with delicious gelato and head hillside to the Church of St.George for stunning views. The setting of the harbour is spectacular and the locals so welcoming, it is well recommended to spend some time soaking up the atmosphere.

stops.heading: rapallo
stops.text: With a nostalgic air, the palm-lined beach, trompe l’oeil façades and seaside 16th-century castle all add to Rapallo’s appeal. Waterfront restaurants create a lively dining scene, the fascinating monastery of San Fruttuoso is best visited by yacht and don’t miss taking the local funivia (cable railway) up to the stunning Sanctuary of Montallegro with spectacular views. For the ultimate beach experience, Silent Bay at Sestri Levanti ticks all the boxes. A locals favourite, houses tumble down to the golden sands and colourful fishing boats dot the shoreline. Ashore there are boutiques and gelato shops to discover in the bustling old town.

stops.heading: cingue terre
stops.text: Directly translated, Cinque Terre means ‘Five Lands’; namely the coastal villages of Monterosso al Mare, Vernazza, Corniglia, Manarola, and Riomaggiore. This unique region is part of the Cinque Terre National Park and is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Here, hilltop houses are painted in a range of vivid colours so that local fishermen can see their homes from the sea. No big label shops will take your attention from the main event: lunch. Meander through the narrow streets, stop and sip an ice-cold limoncello and soak up the laid back atmosphere with a plate of fresh antipasti. Here’s a place to slow down and watch the world go by.

stops.heading: portovenere
stops.text: Nestled in the Bay of Poets, a yachting haven, picturesque Portovenere is adorned with traditional gelato-coloured buildings. Approaching from the water, the quaint harbour is surrounded by old fishermen's houses and interspersed with lively cafés. This charming medieval village offers a slice of fascinating culture - a great place for wandering and to soak up the relaxed atmosphere. Wind your way up the cobbled alleys from the harbour to find great views at the castle and take lunch at one of the excellent local restaurants where freshly caught fish is always on the menu.

stops.heading: forte dei marmi
stops.text: Renowned for its vast expanse of sandy beaches, Forte dei Marmi is a popular seaside region on the Tuscan coast. Characterised by The Pontile, this long, central pier offers wide views across the Tyrrhenian Sea and back towards the city flanked by the Apuan Alps. Ashore the smart town is a highly stylish zone, the marble streets are lined with fashionable boutiques and designer stores. Enjoy leisurely relaxation on the enchanting 11 kilometres of beach, strewn with chic “bagni” beach clubs offering day to night entertainment. The backdrop of elegant luxury villas that dot the hillsides simply add to the exclusive feel emanating from this vibrant location.

stops.heading: elba
stops.text: The largest island of the Tuscan archipelago, Elba boasts transparent blue waters, lush landscapes and bright buildings thronging with friendly locals. It is no wonder this is a popular place for yacht charters to include on their itinerary. In this little slice of paradise the many beaches offer sand, shingle and pebbles, while scuba diving is excellent thanks to the surrounding well-preserved coral reef. Steeped in history and culture, Portoferraio is one of the oldest regional towns, where buildings display stunning architecture. Soak up panoramas from the top of Monte Capanne accessed by chairlift, or visit Capoliveri, famous for markets and traditional artisan produce.

stops.heading: isola del giglio
stops.text: With a host of sensational beaches boasting crystalline waters, scuba divers, snorkellers and swimmers all relish time on Giglio Island. Porto Santo Stefano stands hillside with an imposing Spanish style fortress that dominates the harbour. Take a wander around the citadel walls and staircases to fully explore the history alongside some incredible views. Do not miss the superb array of beaches here - at Caldane the sand is almost red, influenced by the surrounding rocks while Cannelle is only accessible from the water, so an ideal spot for yachts to anchor in tranquillity.

stops.heading: rome
stops.text: End your Monaco to Rome yacht charter in the Eternal City, a deeply complex and vastly sprawling metropolis that is impossible to appreciate in just one day. However, capturing a few of the highlights on a sightseeing tour is worth planning ahead. Disembarking from your journey from Monaco to Rome, the Colosseum and Forum are amongst the most iconic attractions that await. Throw coins in the Trevi Fountain and you’ll be sure to return to explore more of Rome in the future. As you disembark your luxury yacht charter, make plans to explore ashore in this fascinating part of the world.

mediterranean/france.title: calvi to cala di volpe
intro: Experience the high-life amongst these gorgeous hotspots of the Western Mediterranean, where pretty coastlines and fine dining offer the perfect Italian-French mix for an unforgettable charter.

Modern and elegant, a yacht charter in Corsica and Sardinia is a chic affair: indeed combining both fabulous islands brings about the best of both worlds. Rugged Corsica is an absolute delight with an undulating coastline strewn with fishing villages and sheer beauty at the Scandola Nature Reserve. In addition, Sardinia’s white sand beaches peppered with trendy beach clubs belie the inland riches of fascinating ancient cities and Michelin-starred restaurant.
An itinerary here is a photographer’s paradise: make the most of exceptional panoramic views, many-hues of azure water and architecture to make you step back in time.

stops.heading: calvi to girolata
stops.text: Calvi’s marina is a perfect starting point for your trip, where the dedicated crew members will welcome you on board. A gentle cruise to Golfe of Girolata, a stunning nature reserve with romantic flair, is a lovely setting to enjoy your first afternoon and evening.

stops.heading: girolata - ajaccio
stops.text: Move towards the fascinating birthplace of Napoleon, where you can enjoy a walk through the beautiful old town and discover the scenic ruins of Ajaccio.

stops.heading: ajaccio - bonifacio
stops.text: Head towards the lively, medieval town of Bonifacio after enjoying some entertaining water sports in the morning. This miniature St Tropez has sights to see, streets to stroll and restaurants in which you will find excellent Mediterranean cuisine. Built on eroded limestone, Bonifacio has simply amazing views out to sea.

stops.heading: bonifacio - maddalena islands
stops.text: Cruise to the La Maddalena archipelago, to the north of Sardinia, where an unspoiled area of outstanding natural beauty awaits. Take the tender and explore the little coves and bays: the water here is among the most striking in the West Med.

stops.heading: maddalena islands - porto cervo
stops.text: Anchoring at Porto Cervo, take the opportunity to shop in some chic and exclusive boutiques. Enjoy the sunset with a cocktail whilst watching the world go by before dining at one of the excellent restaurants along the promenade. Don’t forget to dress for the occasion.

stops.heading: porto cervo - cala di volpe
stops.text: Unspoiled beaches call out for swimming while the warm sand is ideal for sunbathing. The bay of Cala di Volpe is perfect for complete and utter relaxation, finished off by drinks and dinner at the Yacht Club Costa Smeralda.

stops.heading: cala di volpe - porto rotondo
stops.text: End your superyacht charter at picturesque Porto Rotondo, where you have the chance to have a last alfresco dinner on board.

mediterranean/greece.title: Rhodes to Bodrum
intro: Providing minimal distances between the islands, a charter across the Dodecanese is filled with beauty off the beaten track.
Boasting an array of islands rich in architectural heritage and scenic beauty, cruising from Rhodes to Bodrum takes in the splendour this region has to offer.

Many islands are uninhabited with secluded anchorages to experience the ultimate in tranquility. Others are thriving with chic boutiques and bustling tavernas where the ouzo flows into the early hours. Cruising here is a diverse blend of Aegean delights, packed with opportunities for adventure.

stops.heading: rhodes
stops.text: Embark in vibrant Rhodes, the largest and historically most important of the Dodecanese islands. The Old Town is a walk-through antiquity, amongst atmospheric cobbled streets flanked by Byzantine buildings. Delivering an ideal beach lifestyle, the 300+ days of sunshine a year benefit a multitude of beautiful bays, swathes of sandy beaches and lively coastal towns. With no shortage of places to visit from the whitewashed charm of Acropolis-topped Lindos to the cosmopolitan resort and watersports draw of Ialissos, Rhodes is packed with appeal. Spend the night in Rhodes harbour.

stops.heading: rhodes to symi
stops.text: Cruise to idyllic Nanou Bay at nearby Symi (20nm – 1hr 25min) for a lunchtime stop with swimming and relaxation in total tranquillity. This secluded and often deserted pebble beach boasts crystal clear waters, perfect for snorkelling and fringed by striking cliffs where amusing local goats roam. Symi is a perfect yachting location due to a wide range of wide bays and coves to explore. Head to spectacular Symi Port (6nm – 30mins) at Gialos, where pastel neoclassical mansions cluster on the hillside around the horseshoe bay. Here the variety of tavernas, bars and cafes strewn along the quayside give a truly cosmopolitan feel. Spend the night here.

stops.heading: symi to arki
stops.text: Set off early from Symi Port to anchor at Arki Island (90nm – 6hr 30min), a small isle to the southwest. The Arki archipelago is a miniature group of uninhabited atolls and rocky reefs. This well-kept secret may be a tiny dot on the map, yet it makes a huge impression. As a hideaway escape Arki is a celebration of nature, with vast stretches of seashore lapped by pristine turquoise waters - Tiganakia beach is a standout spot with no nearby roads where shallow white rocks encircle an exotic sandy swimming area. With only 50 occupants, peace and quiet reign in the nirvana of Arki. Spend the night in Port Augusta, Arki (1nm – 5min) with a handful of lively local tavernas.

stops.heading: arki to lipsi
stops.text: Head for secluded Lipsi (9nm – 40min) a small speck of land surrounded by 24 islets. This dreamy island, ancient home of goddess Kalypso, is an escape to nature in the company of hospitable locals. Famed for sweet local wine, this is celebrated by many festivities during the summer in the form of traditional songs and dances. Indeed, the feast of icon “Panagia” in August lasts 24 hours and is a fascinating experience. Radiating character and charm, Lipsi is ideal for wandering amongst quaint alleyways, enjoying local cuisine and climb to the highest point of the Aravis mill for spectacular views. The sandy beaches at Kampos, Lientou and Katsdia offer hours of tranquil relaxation and endless opportunities for diving and snorkelling in the transparent waters. Amongst the rich flora and fauna found in these islets, enjoy spotting Monachus seals, sea turtles and dolphins. Spend the night in Lipsi Port (3nm – 20min).

stops.heading: lipsi to patmos
stops.text: Make way to Patmos (9nm – 40min), a small seahorse shaped island, not far from the coast of Turkey. Famed as an apocalyptic place where St John was inspired to write the Book of Revelation, this is an island with intense spiritual presence. Walk the paths of the Chora, enjoying exquisite views over the Aegean with the fortress-style monastery perched atop the hill. For eating, drinking and socializing, Agia Levies is the village square to visit, where locals and visitors mix to enjoy lively evenings. Beaches abound on Patmos, a popular choice for families being Kambos due to warm, shallow waters and tamarisk trees for natural shade. This relatively out-of-the-way haven blessed with scenic landscapes and small islands is indeed a yachting paradise. Notably, 8nm (30 min) to the east, is the pinprick-sized island of Marathi, where Pantelis Restaurant serves some of the most delicious seafood in the Dodecanese. Spend the night in Patmos Port (3nm – 20min).

stops.heading: patmos to kos
stops.text: Nearby Leros (16nm – 1hr 20min) is a little piece of Italy in Greece. This unusual island is different to its neighbours, offering secret beaches, laid-back tavernas and fascinating modern history. Alinda Bay offers the longest beach, overlooked by an imposing Byzantine castle and nearby Agia Marina port is great for a leisurely coffee and offers a beautiful beach lined with restaurants. Neighbouring Pserimos, known as the island without streets, is small but striking. Superbly peaceful and dotted with countless inlets, sheltered and uninhabited Plathy has a great anchorage and divers can enjoy exploring two shipwrecks. This is an idyllic location to really kick back and relax, spend time in the sunshine and use all the facilities on board to the max. Make way to overnight in Kos (40nm – 3hrs), an island of many choices, featuring pretty beaches, laid-back villages, bustling shops and lively bars.

stops.heading: kos to bodrum
stops.text: Fringed by spectacular beaches, some offering complete solitude, others populated by lively beach clubs, Kos is an island of untold treasure. Rich with ancient landmarks, specifically around Kos Town, historical ruins, temples, shrines and castles are worth discovering. Anchor at Bubble Beach and swim in to find the sparkling natural springs emerging from under the sand. Ideally admired from on board a yacht, the landscape of Kos is breath-taking with attractive villages, verdant hills and charming coastal towns. Watersports abound and there are many bays to anchor and take to the water for some relaxation and fun. Inland, Zia is a tiny mountainous village with incredible views over the sea and traditional tavernas specifically placed to make the most of the legendary sunset. Cruise to Bodrum (10nm – 1hr) for clearance after which find a good spot to enjoy some relaxed swimming. Spend the night in port

stops.heading: bodrum
stops.text: With its palm-lined streets, the elegant seaside resort of Bodrum is packed with chic boutiques and lively restaurants. From the top of the castle to the glittering marina, this popular town radiates a cool, cosmopolitan vibe. Soak up the atmosphere from your yacht, relaxing in the sunshine or exploring the town further before disembarkation at your leisure.

mediterranean/greece.teaser: Providing minimal distances between the islands, a charter across the Dodecanese is filled with beauty off the beaten track.

mediterranean/greece.title: corfu to zakynthos
intro: Embark on a voyage through mythical history and magical beaches in the Ionian with our Corfu to Zakynthos yacht charter. These incredible islands have a slightly cooler climate than much of Greece. The forested mountainsides whisper tales of Homer, and the archipelagos are blessed with lush greenery, cool waters and a wealth of marine life.

Cruise past islands covered in cypress and pine trees and contrasting towns with dappled red-tiles simmering in the sunshine. The Ionian is packed with characteristics that make sailing from Corfu to Zante (aka Zakynthos) a magical experience. With many beautiful ports offering nearby tavernas and hillsides dotted with ancient ruins, take a relaxed island-hopping adventure on your yacht charter from Corfu, and make the most of access from the water. Discover small caves and explore secluded bays, enjoy playing with the watersports toys in tranquillity and don't forget to take in some sublime sunsets.

stops.heading: corfu
stops.text: The Ionian’s most famous island is as described in the mythical sea adventure of Homer’s Odyssey. Now a World Heritage Site, the cultural highlight is its old town, which is surrounded by impressive fortifications, and surrounded by beautiful bays and wildflower countryside. Discover Corfu's UNESCO-listed historic centre, stroll through its charming streets, savour the local cuisine, and immerse yourself in the vibrant nightlife before settling back on your luxury yacht for the night.

stops.heading: corfu - paxos
stops.text: Sail across to Paxos and take the tender ashore to see the Emritis Cliffs, on the northwest coast of the island. There are countless small coves and beaches, and your Captain will know the best places to relax, swim, snorkel and sunbathe. Experience the untouched charm of Paxos, explore its olive groves, and dine in traditional Greek tavernas, enjoying mouth-watering local dishes.

stops.heading: paxos - anti paxos - levkas
stops.text: Before anchoring in Levkas, don’t miss the chance to visit the tiny neighbouring island of Anti Paxos and let your family and friends try out the toys on board with some fast and furious watersports in the crystalline waters. Relish the tranquillity of the unspoiled beaches and the aquamarine waters that Anti Paxos has to offer before setting sail for Levkas.

stops.heading: levkas - meganissi - levkas
stops.text: Characterized by wooded hills with lush greenery as well as an awe-inspiring coastline dotted with high cliffs, Levkas is a heaven for hikers as well as watersports fanatics. The islet of Meganissi just south of Levkas is an excellent place for swimming, diving, snorkelling and fishing as well as taking long lunches in the port. Experience the untouched beauty of Meganissi's beaches, enjoy traditional Greek cuisine in the quaint port, and end the day with a serene sunset on board your luxury yacht.

stops.heading: levkas - ithaca
stops.text: Discover the renowned home of the legendary Odysseus. Ithaca is the historical and cultural pearl of the Ionians. Explore the fountain of Arethusa and the cave of the Nymphs. Relax on its secluded beaches and enjoy the peaceful charm that resonates from this mesmerising island.

stops.heading: ithaca - kefalonia
stops.text: Cruise to Fiskardo, a beautiful harbour in the north of Cephalonia, whose waters are decorated by elegant yachts and has arguably the most stylish fishing port in the Ionian Sea. Explore the picturesque streets of Fiskardo, lined with Venetian-style houses, chic boutiques, and vibrant bars and restaurants.

stops.heading: kefalonia - zakynthos
stops.text: The last stop during you trip will be to the flower of the east, named by the Venetians who were impressed by Zakynthos’ natural beauty and wildflowers. Take the chance to kick back on pristine beaches, and visit a natural miracle at the Blue Caves. End your Corfu to Zakynthos yacht charter by immersing in the vibrancy of Zante's nightlife, visiting its iconic landmarks, or simply relaxing on your superyacht while watching the sun dip into the horizon.

mediterranean/greece.title: Cyclades Itinerary
intro: The beauty of chartering in the Cyclades is the freedom to hop between islands, depending on where the mood takes you. The warm, calm waters are a huge draw alongside the relaxed vibe emanating from the coastal towns.

As with other Aegean islands, the Cyclades sit in the route of the warm Meltemi wind, from the end of June and through to September. So, whilst experiencing the beauty and romance of the Cyclades, this is the time to enjoy some excellent sailing.

stops.heading: athens to kea
stops.text: Start your cruise at the ancient port of Athens and move to Kea, a rocky island ideal for hiking due to its varied landscapes, from orchards and coves to vineyards and valleys. End your day with a swim in warm, azure waters.

stops.heading: kea to sifnos
stops.text: Cruise to Sifnos and explore the stunning circular archipelago with your yacht and tenders. Take time on shore to visit the beautiful village of Castro and drop anchor to enjoy complete tranquility in one of numerous hidden bays.

stops.heading: sifnos to milos
stops.text: Anchor at Milos and spend the day playing in the water. Paddleboarding, swimming and snorkelling are all excellent options here, where the water is gin-clear.

stops.heading: milos to santorini
stops.text: Shaped by an enormous volcanic explosion, Santorini became a flooded crescent-shaped caldera: the inspiration for the myth of Atlantis. Not just famous for its volcano, Santorini is well-known for scenic beaches, such as the black pebble beach of Kamari, where you can anchor and enjoy the water. Don’t miss the chance to visit Oia to watch the breath-taking sunset, arguably the world’s most beautiful.

stops.heading: Santorini to Ios
stops.text: Anchor at Ios, a magically tranquil place. Have a BBQ on board and enjoy the Mediterranean sun with a good book on the aft deck.

stops.heading: Ios to Paros
stops.text: One of the most popular Greek Islands, Paros will be a highlight of your superyacht charter. The stunning beaches and guaranteed light breezes make it ideal for windsurfing and kitesurfing.

stops.heading: paros to mykonos
stops.text: Cruise to the Ibiza of Greece where traditional Greek myths and history mixes with cosmopolitan culture and fun. Visit the location of the great battle between Zeus and the Titans, enjoy the vibrant nightlife of Chora, and soak up the view of this lovely island from the privacy of your yacht.

stops.heading: mykonos to athens
stops.text: Visit the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis, Delos, then explore some of Greece’s rich cultural heritage in Syros, before cruising back to Athens.

mediterranean/italy.title: Rome to Naples
intro: The Italian Amalfi coastline is a yachting haven, offering a variety of exceptional anchorages, fabulous cuisine, coastal towns and picturesque fishing villages. This is a wonderful location to experience la dolce vita while on a yacht charter.

Entering into Civitavecchia by yacht is special. Rome needs no introduction, tradition, history and culture say it all. Dine in style amidst architecture of days gone by, marvel at the multitude of breath-taking sights and become immersed in the wonderful Italian lifestyle bursting with huge personality.

Steeped in history, the wide Gulf of Naples is a panoramic bay fringed by the islands of Capri, Ischia and Procida, where visitors can discover monuments, sweeping scenery and the classic Italian way of life. Achingly romantic with unique allure, the Amalfi Coast offers an idyllic location, with rugged peaks and clifftop palazzos providing a cinematic backdrop for cruising

stops.heading: rome
stops.text: Impossible to appreciate in just one day, Rome offers an enormous amount to do and see. The Eternal City is deeply complex and vastly sprawling. However just capturing a few of the highlights on a sightseeing tour may be worth planning ahead. The Colosseum and Forum are amongst the most iconic attractions that can easily be viewed. If you throw coins in the Trevi Fountain you’ll be sure to return to explore the delights of Rome in the future. Alternatively coastal Rome has huge appeal with a range of beaches and waterfront entertainment available such as Anzio located slightly south.

stops.heading: ponza
stops.text: Clandestine and inviting, the rugged island of Ponza is a tranquil yachting haven where windless coves dot the coastline. This crescent shaped island rises from the water with rocky hills covered in verdant scrub and brightly coloured houses cluster in quaint towns. Casual restaurants deliver understated aperitifs and delicious fresh fare; this is a place to relish unmitigated Italian charm with laid-back simplicity. Take this opportunity to mess around on the water with THUMPER’s large array of water toys. After a fun-filled day, spend the evening enjoying an al fresco dinner in the company of your guests and watch the beautiful sunset.

stops.heading: ischia
stops.text: Volcanic Ischia is steeped in ancient mythology and famed for its hot thermal springs. The interior boasts lush semi-tropical vegetation with a fascinating mix of vineyards and quirky towns across the landscape. Visit designer boutiques along Via Roma, stroll through the gorgeous Mortella Gardens and relax in traffic-free Sant’Angelo.

stops.heading: capri
stops.text: Small in size, but huge in personality – the exclusive island of Capri is a buzzing, cosmopolitan hub. The playground of discerning Italian gentry, Capri has excellent hotels, restaurants and boutiques. Lively and colourful, whilst also offering spectacular scenery, experience the view from the sheer cliffs of Tiberius’s Leap and visit the natural marvel of the Blue Grotto. Do not miss the sunset at Capri – it is simply breath-taking.

stops.heading: amalfi
stops.text: Make way to the cascading beauty of Amalfi and anchor off Nerano- maybe take lunch at Maria Grazia Restaurant - renowned for spaghetti with zucchini and the friendliness of the owners. Amalfi itself is gracefully picturesque, dotted with clusters of pastel buildings ambling up the hillside. At Cape Conca, the Emerald Grotto is one of Amalfi’s natural wonders. Emitting an eerie emerald hue emanating from its depths thanks to light refracting from an underwater crevice. Hidden coves and sandy bays abound – take time to enjoy the water and simply relaxing in this charming haven.

stops.heading: sorrento
stops.text: With spectacular views over the Bay of Naples, the historic seaside town of Sorrento is packed with picturesque charm. Wander at leisure through the labyrinth of intricate shopping lanes then head to the picturesque fishing quarter at Marina Grande where you can enjoy delicious fresh seafood for lunch on the waterfront. Close to the harbour, the small and sandy beach at Marina Piccola is a popular choice or slightly further south, Punto del Capo, is an attractive option. Adventurous visitors should not pass up a trip to the striking ruins of Vesuvius and Pompeii if time permits

stops.heading: naples
stops.text: Steeped in antiquity, Naples is filled with fascinating culture. The city centre is the largest area of protected history within Europe, spanning 27 centuries. The architecture, monuments and stories that surround this city are simply fascinating. Home of the margherita pizza, stop at one of the bustling restaurants to sample this local delight.

mediterranean/italy.teaser: The Italian Amalfi coastline is a yachting haven, offering a variety of exceptional anchorages, fabulous cuisine, coastal towns and picturesque fishing villages. This is a wonderful location to experience la dolce vita while on a yacht charter.

mediterranean/italy.title: calvi to cala di volpe
intro: Experience the high-life amongst these gorgeous hotspots of the Western Mediterranean, where pretty coastlines and fine dining offer the perfect Italian-French mix for an unforgettable charter.

Modern and elegant, a yacht charter in Corsica and Sardinia is a chic affair: indeed combining both fabulous islands brings about the best of both worlds. Rugged Corsica is an absolute delight with an undulating coastline strewn with fishing villages and sheer beauty at the Scandola Nature Reserve. In addition, Sardinia’s white sand beaches peppered with trendy beach clubs belie the inland riches of fascinating ancient cities and Michelin-starred restaurant.
An itinerary here is a photographer’s paradise: make the most of exceptional panoramic views, many-hues of azure water and architecture to make you step back in time.

stops.heading: calvi to girolata
stops.text: Calvi’s marina is a perfect starting point for your trip, where the dedicated crew members will welcome you on board. A gentle cruise to Golfe of Girolata, a stunning nature reserve with romantic flair, is a lovely setting to enjoy your first afternoon and evening.

stops.heading: girolata - ajaccio
stops.text: Move towards the fascinating birthplace of Napoleon, where you can enjoy a walk through the beautiful old town and discover the scenic ruins of Ajaccio.

stops.heading: ajaccio - bonifacio
stops.text: Head towards the lively, medieval town of Bonifacio after enjoying some entertaining water sports in the morning. This miniature St Tropez has sights to see, streets to stroll and restaurants in which you will find excellent Mediterranean cuisine. Built on eroded limestone, Bonifacio has simply amazing views out to sea.

stops.heading: bonifacio - maddalena islands
stops.text: Cruise to the La Maddalena archipelago, to the north of Sardinia, where an unspoiled area of outstanding natural beauty awaits. Take the tender and explore the little coves and bays: the water here is among the most striking in the West Med.

stops.heading: maddalena islands - porto cervo
stops.text: Anchoring at Porto Cervo, take the opportunity to shop in some chic and exclusive boutiques. Enjoy the sunset with a cocktail whilst watching the world go by before dining at one of the excellent restaurants along the promenade. Don’t forget to dress for the occasion.

stops.heading: porto cervo - cala di volpe
stops.text: Unspoiled beaches call out for swimming while the warm sand is ideal for sunbathing. The bay of Cala di Volpe is perfect for complete and utter relaxation, finished off by drinks and dinner at the Yacht Club Costa Smeralda.

stops.heading: cala di volpe - porto rotondo
stops.text: End your superyacht charter at picturesque Porto Rotondo, where you have the chance to have a last alfresco dinner on board.

mediterranean/italy.title: monaco to rome
intro: The Italian coastline is a wonderful yacht charter destination, filled with diversity and something special to please all tastes. Whether seeking a romantic getaway, a multi-generational family holiday or time with good friends, there is magic to be found on your Monaco to Rome yacht itinerary.

From glittering Monaco to the charms of chic Portofino, the colourful appeal of Cinque Terre to the beauty of Elba, cruising these endless coastal delights on board a luxury yacht is an exhilarating journey from Monaco to Italy. The Italian Riviera, a stunning stretch from Monaco to Rome, is renowned for its mild climate, prolific heritage sites and classical atmosphere; the perfect destination to experience an unforgettable luxury yacht charter.

stops.heading: monaco
stops.text: Embark your yacht in the glittering port of Monaco. The principality of Monaco is the world’s second smallest country, making up for its size with immense personality. Sitting atop narrow coastal area with three sides bounded by France and facing the dazzling Mediterranean, it is an inexcusably thrilling destination. As your Monaco to Rome yacht charter sets sail, marvel at one of the most beautiful harbours set against dramatic cliffs and brimming with mega yachts, exuding an aura of exclusive elegance.

stops.heading: portofino
stops.text: Vibrant and charming, Portofino is a splash of colourful houses sat against a riot of lush hillside greenery and sapphire blue waters. Renowned for emanating style, the beating heart is the piazzetta, nestling in a small coastal nook, teeming with chic bars, boutiques and restaurants. Luxury yachts bob in the sparkling bay and anchorages abound. Enjoy a leisurely stroll, refresh with delicious gelato and head hillside to the Church of St.George for stunning views. The setting of the harbour is spectacular and the locals so welcoming, it is well recommended to spend some time soaking up the atmosphere.

stops.heading: rapallo
stops.text: With a nostalgic air, the palm-lined beach, trompe l’oeil façades and seaside 16th-century castle all add to Rapallo’s appeal. Waterfront restaurants create a lively dining scene, the fascinating monastery of San Fruttuoso is best visited by yacht and don’t miss taking the local funivia (cable railway) up to the stunning Sanctuary of Montallegro with spectacular views. For the ultimate beach experience, Silent Bay at Sestri Levanti ticks all the boxes. A locals favourite, houses tumble down to the golden sands and colourful fishing boats dot the shoreline. Ashore there are boutiques and gelato shops to discover in the bustling old town.

stops.heading: cingue terre
stops.text: Directly translated, Cinque Terre means ‘Five Lands’; namely the coastal villages of Monterosso al Mare, Vernazza, Corniglia, Manarola, and Riomaggiore. This unique region is part of the Cinque Terre National Park and is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Here, hilltop houses are painted in a range of vivid colours so that local fishermen can see their homes from the sea. No big label shops will take your attention from the main event: lunch. Meander through the narrow streets, stop and sip an ice-cold limoncello and soak up the laid back atmosphere with a plate of fresh antipasti. Here’s a place to slow down and watch the world go by.

stops.heading: portovenere
stops.text: Nestled in the Bay of Poets, a yachting haven, picturesque Portovenere is adorned with traditional gelato-coloured buildings. Approaching from the water, the quaint harbour is surrounded by old fishermen's houses and interspersed with lively cafés. This charming medieval village offers a slice of fascinating culture - a great place for wandering and to soak up the relaxed atmosphere. Wind your way up the cobbled alleys from the harbour to find great views at the castle and take lunch at one of the excellent local restaurants where freshly caught fish is always on the menu.

stops.heading: forte dei marmi
stops.text: Renowned for its vast expanse of sandy beaches, Forte dei Marmi is a popular seaside region on the Tuscan coast. Characterised by The Pontile, this long, central pier offers wide views across the Tyrrhenian Sea and back towards the city flanked by the Apuan Alps. Ashore the smart town is a highly stylish zone, the marble streets are lined with fashionable boutiques and designer stores. Enjoy leisurely relaxation on the enchanting 11 kilometres of beach, strewn with chic “bagni” beach clubs offering day to night entertainment. The backdrop of elegant luxury villas that dot the hillsides simply add to the exclusive feel emanating from this vibrant location.

stops.heading: elba
stops.text: The largest island of the Tuscan archipelago, Elba boasts transparent blue waters, lush landscapes and bright buildings thronging with friendly locals. It is no wonder this is a popular place for yacht charters to include on their itinerary. In this little slice of paradise the many beaches offer sand, shingle and pebbles, while scuba diving is excellent thanks to the surrounding well-preserved coral reef. Steeped in history and culture, Portoferraio is one of the oldest regional towns, where buildings display stunning architecture. Soak up panoramas from the top of Monte Capanne accessed by chairlift, or visit Capoliveri, famous for markets and traditional artisan produce.

stops.heading: isola del giglio
stops.text: With a host of sensational beaches boasting crystalline waters, scuba divers, snorkellers and swimmers all relish time on Giglio Island. Porto Santo Stefano stands hillside with an imposing Spanish style fortress that dominates the harbour. Take a wander around the citadel walls and staircases to fully explore the history alongside some incredible views. Do not miss the superb array of beaches here - at Caldane the sand is almost red, influenced by the surrounding rocks while Cannelle is only accessible from the water, so an ideal spot for yachts to anchor in tranquillity.

stops.heading: rome
stops.text: End your Monaco to Rome yacht charter in the Eternal City, a deeply complex and vastly sprawling metropolis that is impossible to appreciate in just one day. However, capturing a few of the highlights on a sightseeing tour is worth planning ahead. Disembarking from your journey from Monaco to Rome, the Colosseum and Forum are amongst the most iconic attractions that await. Throw coins in the Trevi Fountain and you’ll be sure to return to explore more of Rome in the future. As you disembark your luxury yacht charter, make plans to explore ashore in this fascinating part of the world.

mediterranean/malta.title: Aeolian Islands: Catania to Palermo
intro: Once the haunt of ancient deities, the beautiful Aeolian Islands in the Tyrrhenian Sea are now worshipped for their raw natural beauty and glittering nightlife.

The Aeolians, seven volcanic islands adrift in the Tyrrhenian Sea, are a spectacle of nature's raw power and beauty. Named after Aeolus, the ancient Greek god of the winds, these islands are a mosaic of otherworldly landscapes. Smouldering volcanoes, therapeutic mud baths, and beaches where black sands meet turquoise waves.

Here, island hopping becomes an art form, every view is a masterpiece, every meal a feast of local tradition. This is Italy intensified, and a place where a luxury yacht charter truly comes into its own.

Between scaling live volcanoes, bathing in freshwater springs and visiting local vineyards to sample “the wine of the volcanoes”, you’ll cruise between these stunning islands, anchor in intimate bays, and enjoy your favourite cuisine under the stars, courtesy of your personal chef.

stops.heading: catania
stops.text: Your Aeolian Islands yacht charter begins in an ancient port city on Sicily’s east coast, Catania. A city whose fate and fortune has been sculpted by the infamous Mount Etna over centuries. Built upon the lava stone that once destroyed it. In Goethe’s words, "to have seen Italy without having seen Sicily is not to have seen Italy at all." And for us, to have seen Sicily without having seen Catania is not to have seen Sicily at all. So, we recommend exploring before you set sail. The ancient Roman theatre, impressive Baroque architecture at Piazza del Duomo, and the rowdy fish market. Unadulterated Siciliana is around every corner. Swapping the hustle and bustle of the Amalfi Coast’s famed port towns for intimate anchorages surrounded by sensational natural beauty and rich with authentic Italian charm, once aboard your private yacht and greeted by your crew, your Aeolian yacht charter begins and a short cruise to Taormina awaits.

stops.heading: taormina
stops.text: On your approach to Taormina, you will navigate rocky coves, tiny islands like the famous Isola Bella, and a scattering of sea stacks, making this enchanting coastline a firm favourite with those arriving by yacht. Upon arrival visitors are greeted by a town that epitomises the magic of Sicilian culture. Situated high above the eastern coast, and served by its very own cable car to and from the seaside resorts below, it is easy to see why Taormina has been the most popular tourist destination in Sicily for over 200 years. Ancient terraces, adorned with elegant gardens and chic cafes offer views cascading gracefully down to the Ionian Sea, with Mount Etna (usually smoking) standing proudly in the distance. A vibrant array of shops, bars, and restaurants, set against the backdrop of winding streets, creates a lively yet intimate atmosphere with beautifully restored mediaeval buildings offering a vivid reminder of why this place became a pivotal stop on the Grand Tour. After a day exploring this little Italian gem, settle down for an overnight cruise to the Aeolian islands.

stops.heading: stromboli
stops.text: A yacht charter in the Aeolian Islands is not complete without visiting the magnificent Stromboli. The approach by yacht is spectacular with the sight of its active volcano, a vivid reminder of the island's raw, natural power. Once considered the home of the Greek God Aeolus, Stromboli has transformed into a secluded spot favoured by celebrities, including fashion icons like Dolce and Gabbana. Its appeal lies in its unspoiled beauty and dramatic volcanic displays, especially at night when eruptions light up the sky, best viewed from your yacht. The island's small towns, Ginostra and Scari, offer distinct experiences. Ginostra is the epitome of seclusion, a tiny village with less than 30 inhabitants, perfect for those seeking tranquillity. Scari, on the other hand, leads to San Vincenzo, a picturesque village with whitewashed houses and colourful bougainvillaea, embodying Mediterranean charm. For beach lovers, the northern coast's Ficogrande and Piscità are ideal, boasting beautiful beaches, fine dining, and boutique shopping. This blend of natural beauty and understated elegance makes exploring Stromboli a unique and memorable part of any Aeolian yacht charter.

stops.heading: panarea
stops.text: Known as ‘The VIP Island’, on Day 4 of your Aeolian Islands, immerse yourself in the exclusive allure of Panarea. The Aeolian Islands' smallest yet most fashionable destination was once a tranquil hideaway, but has transformed into a stylish haven following the arrival of Paolo Tilche and Myriam Beltrami in 1958, a change marked by the iconic Hotel Raya. The island's coastline, though lacking traditional sandy beaches, offers its own charm with rocky inlets and crystal-clear waters, the perfect playground for those on a luxury yacht charter. Anchor off Cala Junco beach and visit the peaceful cove at Le Guilie. Enjoy a serene swim or stroll along the coast to Punta Milazzese, where Bronze Age settlement foundations perch atop the headland. Take a walk through the whitewashed streets in San Pietro and soak up the laid back vibe before the sun sets and the island's decadent social scene comes alive. The evening’s passeggiata (evening walk) brings a buzz to the narrow lanes filled with chic boutiques, offering an array of stylish evening and beach wear. The real magic of Panarea's nightlife unfolds in its exclusive clubs and bars, where a bohemian Mediterranean vibe blends with modern luxury. The island's venues, known for their sophisticated ambiance and high-profile clientele, are sure to impress.

stops.heading: lipari
stops.text: Lipari, the largest of the Aeolian Islands, defies its reputation as just a transport hub, revealing a vibrant blend of history, culture, and natural beauty. The island's heart, Lipari Town, is a treasure trove of history, evident in its richly stocked Aeolian Museum, and a culinary hotspot, boasting renowned establishments like Ristorante da Filippino. Founded in 1910, this restaurant is famed for its exquisite local dishes, such as raviolini of grouper, offering a taste of authentic Aeolian cuisine. The island's natural allure is epitomised by Spiaggia Bianca di Pomici in the north.
