Heading north, the coastline tells tales of ancient rainforests while vibrant marine life thrives below. As the sun melts over the horizon, the pristine waters around the Butang Islands beckon. Anchoring here promises serene views and the anticipation of the six days of luxury and discovery that lie ahead.

stops.heading: the butang islands
stops.text: The Butang Islands, protected by the Tarutao National Marine Park, comprise over 50 individual isles. Each provides unique diving spots, pristine beaches, and quiet coves. Accessible primarily by yacht, these islands promise both exclusivity and raw natural beauty. Divers will appreciate the islands' underwater biodiversity. Here, a quarter of the world's tropical fish species thrive, making it a vibrant mosaic of marine life. Dive deep and you'll likely spot angelfish, trumpetfish, and, if you're lucky, playful dolphins curiously circling. After an invigorating dive, consider a brief visit to the 'sea gypsy' villages of Ko Lipe. Immerse in local culture, maybe even pick up a culinary trick or two. Back on your yacht, as the chef grills a fresh catch of red snapper or kingfish, reflect on the day’s adventure.

stops.heading: the butang islands to krabi
stops.text: Embark on the third day of your Thailand yacht charter with a serene sail to Krabi. Here, the waters offer unparalleled snorkelling and diving amid the majestic green-capped monolithic rock formations synonymous with the region. Witness the marine life up close in a location that sets the gold standard for Thailand's underwater attractions, or simply take in the awe-inspiring scenery. As you explore Krabi expect a blend of natural beauty and refined luxury. Peppered with world-renowned beaches like Railay and bustling hubs such as Ao Nang. With over 80 offshore islands, including Koh Phi Phi made famous by Leo Di Caprio’s “the beach”, a Thailand yacht charter presents a truly unique yachting experience. Here, relaxation and adventure come in equal measure. Spend long afternoons lounging on velvet beaches or explore the mainland where vibrant markets, exclusive dining spots, and select boutiques await. Whether you're after gourmet meals and white glove service or an evening at a private beach club, Krabi ensures your yacht charter in Thailand delivers at every turn.

stops.heading: krabi to koh hong
stops.text: This unique island group is best explored by yacht. On arrival in Koh Hong, anchoring and taking to the water via kayak allows visitors to enter a natural hong (room) that houses a stunning lagoon encircled with towering limestone cliffs and an opening to the sky. A setting where a ballet of longtail boats and speedboats skim the water, bringing day-trippers for fleeting visits. Aboard your private yacht, you'll be privy to an extended soiree. Noisy tuk-tuks are replaced by the rhythmic paddle of your kayak weaving through verdant mangroves, and thriving street markets are traded for local delicacies, where fishermen, in time-honoured tradition, serve just-caught seafood straight from their boats. While popular spots like Railay may brim with energy, Koh Hong offers true escapism, far from the usual buzz of Thai hotspots.

stops.heading: koh hong to koh racha
stops.text: Situated just 12 nautical miles south of Phuket, cruise to Koh Racha through a tricolour of bright-white sand, emerald-green water and cobalt-blue sky. Without doubt best experienced from the deck of a private superyacht, the archipelago consists of two main islands: Koh Racha Yai and Koh Racha Noi. The former is the larger of the two islands offering pristine beaches and vibrant reefs perfect for snorkelling. While those looking for a deeper dive will find solace on the less inhabited Koh Racha Noi where swimming with manta rays is the norm. While Koh Racha's nightlife is subdued with a select few restaurants and bars, its charm lies in its tranquil atmosphere. With minimal artificial lights, stargazing becomes an evening highlight. Enjoy this spectacle either from a quiet beach or your yacht's deck, cocktail in hand.

stops.heading: koh racha to phuket
stops.text: On the final day of your Thailand yacht charter, watch from the fore deck of your superyacht as the 'Pearl of the Andaman,' Phuket, majestically comes into view. The perfect finale to an extraordinary adventure, Phuket offers a plethora of experiences to truly immerse oneself in local culture and history. With an array of world-class resorts beckoning and the convenience of an international airport, many opt to prolong their stay after disembarking, fully soaking in this vibrant metropolis. The silhouette of the Big Buddah stands sentinel, a testimony to the island's rich heritage. From the exhilarating bird's eye view on a helicopter tour to the sacred corridors of Wat Chalong Temple, every corner promises discovery. Whether you're living in a Thai postcard aboard a traditional long-tail boat, exploring the timeless allure of Ranong day market, or in the tranquil embrace of the local Elephant Sanctuary, Phuket is a city of contrasts. In a realm where luxury and adventure combine, our luxury yacht charters in Thailand offer an experience that not only meets but transcends expectations. While your charter may conclude, the memories forged here are eternal.

south-east-asia/thailand.teaser: This itinerary is a blend of two stunning countries in South East Asia. Malaysia and Thailand's beautiful islands will deliver a host of amazing beaches, dive sites, and scenic beauty along the way.

south-pacific/fiji.title: Fiji Itinerary
intro: Overflowing with experiences, Fiji is a versatile getaway in paradise, and our Fiji itinerary is designed to showcase the best it offers. Whether you seek world-class diving, jungle trekking, sheer relaxation on the beach or family activities during your Fiji islands itinerary, you will find it here.

Embrace romance, relaxation, and escapism cruising around this lush group of islands. Meet the locals, retaining a strong sense of tradition, learn about their culture, and enjoy time with some of the friendliest people in the world. Your Fiji islands itinerary is bound to create memories that will last a lifetime.

The allure of the transparently clear aquamarine water is ever-present on this Fiji itinerary. From swimming, snorkelling, diving to kayaking and sailing, every drop of adventure awaits. And yes, cooling off under an enchanting waterfall is a must!

stops.heading: denarau marina to the mamanuca islands
stops.text: Start your Fiji itinerary with a short 1.5-hour cruise southwest to the Mamanuca Islands. Anchor in the lee of Tavarua Island, the heart of Fiji's surfing capital. With iconic surf breaks like ‘Cloud’ and ‘Restaurant’, you’re set for a memorable experience. Even if surfing isn’t your calling, the beauty of these islands alone offers a breathtaking start. Should the weather be uncooperative, a brief one-hour journey will bring you to the Malolo Island lagoon, where you can explore the renowned Muscat Cove Resort and Marina.

stops.heading: malolo and tavarua islands
stops.text: Your Fiji islands itinerary introduces you to the white sandy beaches of Malolo and Tavarua islands. Here, you have the freedom to surf, swim, snorkel, shop, or simply sightsee. Perhaps you'd fancy a stroll on the sandy shores or a cool dip at the sand bar. The Cloud 9 Platform invites you to sip a cocktail as you admire the iconic Cloud break. And as the sun sets, consider a visit to the local beach bar for a mesmerising view.

stops.heading: navadra and vanua islands
stops.text: Continuing our Fiji itinerary, post breakfast, indulge in a morning swim or catch a wave before setting sail to the picturesque Navadra and Vanua Islands. These gems offer stunning beaches and snorkeling spots. Depending on the tides, paddleboards or kayaks might be your ticket to the shores. The Fijian villagers might also offer you a warm invitation to explore their village and partake in an authentic kava ceremony.

stops.heading: naviti island
stops.text: Wake up in paradise on this day of your Fiji islands itinerary, either by Navadra Island or in the sheltered waters of Yalobi Bay. After rejuvenating with a morning swim and breakfast, navigate north to Cuvu Bay on Naviti Island. This sanctuary offers a rare chance to swim with manta rays and promises enchanting snorkeling experiences.

stops.heading: the blue lagoon
stops.text: A gem in our Fiji itinerary, discover the renowned Blue Lagoon, the backdrop of the iconic 1980s film “The Blue Lagoon” starring Brooke Shields. Here, pristine beaches, mesmerising snorkelling spots, and scenic hikes await you. Nearby Sawa-i-lau boasts fascinating underwater caves, a must-visit during your luxury yacht charter.

stops.heading: yasawa island and champagne beach
stops.text: After your customary morning routines, relocate north to Yasawa-i-Ra. Its crown jewel, Champagne Beach, beckons. Relish a beach picnic or BBQ organised just for you by the charter crew. As evening descends, immerse yourself in a traditional Fijian dance, the Meke, and perhaps partake in another Kava ceremony.

stops.heading: island hopping
stops.text: Tailor your Fiji itinerary as you sail south towards Denarau Marina. Revisit cherished spots or uncover new coves like Somosomo Bay or Paradise Cove. Each day is a new opportunity to delve deeper into the Fijian islands' treasures.

stops.heading: vomo island
stops.text: Vomo Island, a serene anchor point in your Fiji yacht charter, promises pure relaxation. With no resorts or villages in sight, enjoy a tranquil stroll on the beach. Consider a hike up Mt Vomo for a 360-degree panorama. Whether snorkelling, swimming, or paddleboarding, embrace the serenity that Vomo offers.

stops.heading: namotu island
stops.text: Wrap up your Fiji itinerary at Namotu Island on the captivating Roro Reef. Renowned for surfing, diving, and more, let the day's catch be your gourmet treat as you unwind in the exquisite anchorage this island affords.

south-pacific/fiji.teaser: Packed with experiences, Fiji is a versatile getaway in paradise. Whether you seek world-class diving, jungle trekking, sheer relaxation on the beach or family activities, you will find it here.

australia-and-new-zealand/australia/the-.title: The Kimberley
intro: Travel around the north-western edge of Australia to discover a raw, wild coastline dotted with some 2600 beautiful islands. The Kimberley, tucked away in the faraway north-west pocket of Australia, is one of the most pristine regions in the world.
Brimming with Australia’s best outback scenery and wildlife, inhabited by just over 50,000 people over 400,000km2, this region is one of the most secluded and scarcely populated in the world.

Reputed as one of Australia’s great natural wonders, discover a never-ending haven of turquoise waters, white sands, waterfalls, and sandstone gorges that will take your breath away. Witness landscapes that have been carved over millions of years, immersed in the diverse wildlife and serenity of the region. Despite the remoteness, this is also a place of great cuisine, friendly locals and one of the most romantic beach towns in the world.

stops.heading: cygnet bay & buccaneer archipelago
stops.text: Your Kimberley adventure starts with a cruise through the islands of King Sound. Take a tender excursion to the Buccaneer Archipelago to witness the ‘giant tides’ where you can watch spectacular whirlpools and overflows being produced. After the exciting tour, head back on board for some relaxing with a cocktail on deck to enjoy your first stunning Kimberley sunset.

stops.heading: king sound to silver gull creek
stops.text: Depart from Cygnet Bay early and cruise across King Sound to uninhabited Hidden Island. Anchor off Silica Beach, one of a kind in The Kimberley, this beach is made from pure, white silica sand making it powder-soft. Spend time here swimming in the turquoise waters and exploring the coastline. At sunset cruise on to your overnight anchorage at the tranquil and remote Silver Gull Creek. Taking dinner on deck, look out for shooting stars in the vast open sky.

stops.heading: cockatoo island to the horizontal falls
stops.text: In the morning cruise past Cockatoo and Koolan Island, both of which are famed for their rich, high grade iron ore, clearly marked by the mining operations that have been established here for decades. Continue to Talbot Bay and head on to the Horizontal Falls which is one of the most breath-taking natural wonders in the Kimberley. Millions of litres of ocean are sucked through a narrow sea gorge at the mouth, where tides as high as 13m push through the two rusty red craggy walls. Affectionately named “Horries”, this natural phenomenon is unlike any other waterfall, as here the water passes horizontally through the narrow gorges. This is a thrilling ride in a fast tender in the Kimberley, indeed travelling with the flow the water surges so fast it goes downhill! Make way to Talbot Bay for an even more powerful natural creation – Cyclone Creek. The rocks are twisted and buckled, displaying spectacular geology in warped horizontal layers. Despite areas of swirling water, the coral reefs are abundant and look out for the ghostly-pale Tawny Nurse Sharks who regularly visit. Back at the yacht, enjoy sunset in Talbot Bay, your anchorage for the night.

stops.heading: montgomery reef to raft point
stops.text: Journey to Montgomery Reef, a dramatic sight, as the “invisible” reef slowly emerges from the ocean on the falling tide. There is often 10m difference on a single tide, so nearly 5m of reef is gradually exposed within about 2 hours from the ocean, with waterfalls and rivers cutting through the reef. Explore up close and watch sea turtles, sea snakes and dolphins playing in the reef and the several small islands nearby are filled with mangroves, crocodiles and bird life. Cruise to Raft Point for an overnight anchorage. This large formation of ochre sandstone is close to the mouth of Doubtful bay.

stops.heading: raft point
stops.text: Head ashore at Raft Point to visit the cave gallery of spectacular Wandjinas – an array of amazing indigenous rock art. Created hundreds of years ago, your local Aboriginal guide will share fascinating stories with you. During the afternoon, take the tender to Scotties Creek. Head ashore for a walk through the lush rainforest and enjoy swimming in one of the beautiful lagoons there. Return to the yacht for a relaxed sunset and spend overnight at the Raft Point anchorage

stops.heading: raft point to boondook bay
stops.text: An early departure from Raft Point means a morning cruising through spectacular coastal scenery. Make way back towards Boondook Bay where the yacht will anchor for a leisurely lunch. Take the tenders for an afternoon of exploring the islands and coastline or perhaps relax on board, soaking up the sun. Overnight anchorage in Boondook Bay.

stops.heading: boondook bay to cygnet bay
stops.text: Cruise across King Sound and head back to Cygnet Bay. Along the way keep your eyes open for whales and dolphins. Enjoy a final delicious lunch in the gorgeous surroundings of Cygnet Bay. Transfer ashore for ongoing transport.

stops.heading: Felicite Island
stops.text: The amazing resort island of Felicité is a wonderful location for another action packed day of watersports. This lush, granite isle is just a short tender ride from one of the best snorkelling spots in the world where the abundant marine life is fascinating. The luxurious Six Senses private island resort is an idyllic ecological sanctuary, where relaxation is key. From exquisite dining to spa treatments, this is a great spot to indulge in perfect relaxation on powder-white sands.

stops.heading: fregate island
stops.text: Cruise for three hours overnight to spend the last day experiencing the charm of Anse Victorin on the private island resort of Fregate Island. Although small, this beach is simply perfect and no wonder it has been awarded the title of most beautiful beach in the world multiple times. From here surfing with onboard instructors, a last dive or even catching that last tuna is the goal. Take a leisurely four hour cruise back to the main island of Mahé, which can be timed for departure, or enjoy a day back in Saint Anne Marine nature park before heading home.

australia-and-new-zealand/australia/the-.teaser: Travel around the north-western edge of Australia to discover a raw, wild coastline dotted with some 2600 beautiful islands; welcome to The Kimberley.

caribbean/leeward-islands/antigua.title: antigua to st lucia
intro: Both are jewels in the crown of the Caribbean, but this yacht charter from Antigua to St Lucia offers the best of both worlds. Embarking on this journey allows you to answer the age-old question: Antigua or St Lucia? Experience the serene beauty and luxuries of the Leeward Islands.

The stunning Leeward islands of the Caribbean provide an excellent opportunity to enjoy a leisurely cruise amidst secluded tranquility. This route from Antigua to St Lucia provides time to really discover some breath-taking places as you explore this incredible yacht charter destination.

With so many different islands, it would take a very long time to fully discover all of the delightful Leeward Islands. Variety abounds with coral reefs, marine parks and swathes of perfect beaches featuring heavily. Antigua or St Lucia? Both are exceptional in their ways. Snorkelling and diving here are sublime as the underwater world is teeming with marine life. The mild climate and cool constant winds in the Leewards offer some of the best blue-water cruising in the world.

stops.heading: antigua to guadeloupe
stops.text: Embark at Falmouth Harbour on the north west side of the western island. Cruise from here to Guadaloupe and find a sheltered anchorage of choice, where you can enjoy views of the surrounding mountains, lush rain forests and vibrant towns. This is a great area for snorkeling with colourful underwater life amidst crystalline waters. Guadeloupe’s two main islands form the shape of butterfly wings, joined only by bridges and a mangrove swamp. Grand Terre has fabulous beaches teaming with activities and Basse Terre is home to the Parc National, boasting the incredible La Soufriere volcano. Overnight at Deshais Harbour.

stops.heading: guadeloupe
stops.text: In the morning, make way to Isles des Saint’s, a group of islands on the southern end of Guadeloupe with a choice of 2 main anchorages. There is Bourg des Saints on the main island in front of the town and shops, or alternatively, Islet a Cabrit offers a quieter, sheltered anchorage on one of the smaller islands. Both are great places to really enjoy some relaxation while you swim and snorkel the day away.

stops.heading: guadeloupe to dominica
stops.text: Prince Rupert’s Bay is a large natural harbour, set on the northwestern part of the island. It is a great idea to book an organized, guided boat tour up the Indian River surrounded by the rainforest teeming with wildlife. In addition, there is a large town to explore, some great places to snorkel and taking time to simply soak up the atmosphere.

stops.heading: dominica to martinique
stops.text: After breakfast, head to Fort de France for customs clearance then locate a suitable anchorage across from the harbor, near the beach at Anse a L’ane (there is a good choice of places). There are picturesque towns and swathes of velvet beaches ashore. Snorkeling is very good on the outer reefs thanks to the wonderful marine flora and fauna biodiversity.

stops.heading: martinique to st lucia
stops.text: Make way to Marigot Bay and enjoy the sheer tranquility of this beautiful St Lucia yacht charter location. If you head ashore there are some outstanding seafood restaurants or perhaps visit the dive centre at Marigot Beach Club for a fantastic underwater adventure. After lunch, nearby Soufriere, is small town scattered with brightly painted buildings and a bustling seafront. Home to the Diamond Botanical Gardens, this former plantation is bursting with ornamental plants, a waterfall plus geothermal mineral baths. Further inland the cascading Toraille Waterfall is an amazing sight. Anchor overnight near the famous Pitons, which are spectacular volcanic mountain twin peaks.

stops.heading: the pitons to vieux fort
stops.text: Take time to soak up the scenery and explore the Pitons, this world heritage site offers some fantastic walks plus a range of superb diving and snorkeling. Gros Piton, the loftier of the two peaks is climbable for keen hikers and truly affords an ultimate vantage point to view the island. Alternatively, if you are feeling adventurous, a trip by island buggy, a Segway tour or rainforest ziplining can be great fun and will likely cover areas you would not otherwise see. Make way in the evening to Vieux Fort and spend the night in harbour.

stops.heading: vieux fort
stops.text: Situated at the southern end of the island, enjoy the approaching view of mountain ranges and long white sandy beaches plus this area is great for wind and kitesurfing should the mood take you. Perhaps head ashore to Moule a Chique, scenic point, to take advantage of the 360 vistas from this high point. Cruise round to Anse des Sables Beach and drop anchor to enjoy lunch. Disembark at your leisure – Hewanorra International Airport is nearby.

caribbean/leeward-islands/antigua.teaser: The stunning Leeward islands of the Caribbean provide an excellent opportunity to enjoy a leisurely cruise amidst secluded tranquility. Relax as you sail crystal waters surrounded by beauty.

caribbean/leeward-islands/antigua.title: St Maarten to St Maarten
intro: With a fabulous choice of stunning bays, wonderful marinas and exceptional towns to explore, you will be spoiled for choice during this superyacht charter itinerary.

Cruise calm waters to enjoy an island-hopping adventure in paradise. Whether you seek secluded coves, bustling coastal towns, vibrant nightlife or delicious local cuisine - this itinerary has something for everyone.

stops.heading: simpson bay, st maarten
stops.text: Arrive and be escorted to Marina Isle de Sol, Simpson Bay before sailing to Grande Case to spend the evening at anchor. Before or after your dinner on board, venture ashore for an evening drink. Soak up the French ambiance of a coastal town bustling with cafés and quaint restaurants.

stops.heading: simpson bay to grand case
stops.text: Awake to a full array of yacht toys and enjoy the morning in the bay of Grand Case, where there are no restrictions for waterskiing or jet‐skiing. After lunch on board, your crew will take you to meet a private driver for an afternoon of zip‐lining at Loterie Farm. Then sail the 2 hours to St. Barths for a guided tour of the island, or a leisurely hike up to the old fort to take some photos. Shop in the boutiques or enjoy a day of pampering at one of the magnificent spa’s. Dine at The Eden Roc Hotel before heading to Nikki Beach for drinks.

stops.heading: gustavia
stops.text: After choosing your favourite anchorage in St. Barts and enjoying the warm water, head to the island’s capital, Gustavia, and settle for the night.

stops.heading: st barts to barbuda
stops.text: Head off from St Barths to the island of Barbuda, arriving just in time for lunch. Anchor in Low Bay’s aquamarine waters and explore the endless white sand beaches. After lunch, enjoy a full beach setup with beach games and enjoy the water sports on offer. Enjoy sundowners and sunset views from the jacuzzi on the sundeck.

stops.heading: barbuda to st kitts
stops.text: Sail through the night to St. Kitts and anchor in White House Bay, offering total protection from any weather. Venture ashore or use the water toys available. There is a terrific beach bar at Banana Bay for sundowners.

stops.heading: st kitts
stops.text: Head to shore for a 4x4 off‐road tour, bird tour, railway or rainforest tour. Lunch ashore and then take the tender for an afternoon of offshore fishing. The yacht will then set sail while you sleep, so wake up to a brand new anchorage in Anguilla.

stops.heading: anguilla
stops.text: Awake in Rendezvous Bay, Anguilla. Take advantage of the service of the crew and enjoy beachcombing or hit the beach bars. If there are golfers in your party, this is a great opportunity to play. Anchor in Rendezvous Bay for the night.

stops.heading: st maarten
stops.text: Sail through the night towards St. Maarten, arriving at an anchorage to enjoy the final morning of water sports before returning to dock.

caribbean/the-bahamas/abaco-islands.title: Nassau to Nassau
intro: With a bewildering choice of seven hundred islands and innumerable cays, these stunning cruising grounds have so much to offer.

Whether you are looking to dive into the beautiful blue depths or enjoy “catch of the day” for lunch at a local beach cafe, this island-strewn archipelago will not disappoint. History enthusiasts,carnival-seekers or those wanting complete relaxation will find what they are looking for in this multi-faceted paradise.

This itinerary brings all perfect ingredients together for a memorable cruise: short passages between destinations, tranquil seclusion, beautiful scenery, fresh seafood and great watersports opportunities. Combine this with sun, breeze and the Bahamas’ colourful character, and this a recipe for success.

stops.heading: Nassau to Compass Cay
stops.text: Cruise from Nassau to Compass Cay (approx. 70nm) where you can swim with the nurse sharks right in the marina or take a stroll down the quaint nature paths to the secluded beach on the other side. The walkway here is painted with colorful buoys and signage along the way giving you a true local feel. From here you can anchor off near Rocky Dundas Caves. These two caves are hidden inside a large rock with natural skylights at the top. In order to enter the cave you must swim into a shallow hole where you end up inside a cavern of stalactites and stalagmites. It is quite awe inspiring. caribbean/the-bahamas/bimini-islands.title: The Florida Keys
intro: Venture into the mesmerizing waters of the Florida Keys aboard our exclusive Florida Keys yacht charter. Located south of Miami, the Florida Keys encompass more than 40 islands, crafting a Florida Keys itinerary that is a mosaic of the best diving and snorkelling spots in the US.

As you embark on this unique private yacht charter in the Florida Keys, you're introduced to North America's only living coral barrier reef. Stretching across 110 miles, the Florida Keys radiate a distinct charm that has made this a top destination for travelers.
Brimming with adventure, sightseeing, and watersports opportunities, the Keys deliver an idyllic yacht charter experience epitomizing luxury and nature's splendor.

stops.heading: biscayne bay & south beach
stops.text: Embark in Miami and settle into your private yacht charter Florida Keys journey. Cruise around Biscayne Bay and along the Intracoastal Waterway, gliding past stunning celebrity mansions and legendary hotels on Fisher Island, Palm Island and Hibiscus Island. Biscayne Bay National Park is a vast marine reserve, extending to the northernmost Keys with reefs, sandbars and iconic Stiltsville, a group of pastel-coloured, stilted huts, only reachable by yacht. Spend the night in harbour at South Beach with the opportunity to experience the best of vibrant Miami nightlife with some of the best bars and nightclubs to be found.

stops.heading: the keys
stops.text: Cruise south towards the Florida Keys on your luxury Florida Keys yacht charter. Along the way, enjoy a variety of watersports such as waterskiing, wakeboarding and diving. Dolphins are often sighted and there may be the chance to snorkel with these gentle mammals. Anglers will also be delighted by the great fishing - the best catches are found out in the open sea with 600 species populating the waters.

stops.heading: key largo
stops.text: The self-proclaimed dive capital of the world, Key Largo has a wealth of diving and snorkeling opportunities on the huge coral reef. If you wish to explore ashore, there are plenty of activities to enjoy, specifically some excellent golfing plus a wide range of shopping and superb restaurants. Two state parks, a national park plus a national marine sanctuary ensure that Key Largo is a wildlife haven. America’s first underwater park - John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park - provides an amazing array of underwater sea life and colourful coral. As the sun sets, tender out to Indian Key, where you can watch the colours fade from the sky on this stunning natural key.

stops.heading: key west
stops.text: In the early morning, cruise to Key West on your private yacht charter in the Florida Keys. Experience the world-famous Keys hospitality on this tropical island getaway. As the southernmost point in the continental US, Key West boasts clear blue skies and fabulous weather. During the day, enjoy watersports and fishing in the azure waters – and head ashore for golf or to visit the Ernest Hemingway Museum. Once the sun sets - get ready to truly begin your Key West experience. Head to Mallory Square for Sunset Celebrations, an impromptu event that just so happens to take place every day of the week! Mingle with musicians, jugglers, and mime artists as you stroll around past sidewalk cafes, open-air bars and elegant restaurants. This cool, funky vibe is what Key West is all about.

stops.heading: the marquesas keys
stops.text: Further west, cruise to the tranquil Marquesas Keys, a circular group of ten uninhabited islands, surrounded by pristine waters, home to corals and mangroves. This is a great opportunity to venture out by kayak and explore the fascinating environment up close on your Florida Keys yacht charter. Spend the afternoon with the water toys and diving wrecks and reefs, before relaxing on deck with a cocktail in hand to watch the notoriously breath-taking sunset.

stops.heading: the keys
stops.text: Starting the return trip on your curated Florida Keys itinerary, enjoy breakfast al fresco to soak up the stunning scenery. Take time out to stop at some of the smaller Keys that were not visited along the way. Cruise past the Saddlebunch Keys – a group of mesmerising mangrove islands, spot Loggerhead turtles nesting at Coco Plum Beach and consider a visit to Islamorada for the diving museum, state park and dolphin encounters.

stops.heading: miami
stops.text: After a leisurely morning cruise, arrive back in the coastal resort of Miami to disembark from your memorable Florida Keys yacht charter. Perhaps conclude your trip with a visit to the Art Deco district of diverse Miami Beach, boasting eclectic architecture and a thriving arts centre.

caribbean/the-windward-islands/st-vincen.title: antigua to st lucia
intro: Both are jewels in the crown of the Caribbean, but this yacht charter from Antigua to St Lucia offers the best of both worlds. Embarking on this journey allows you to answer the age-old question: Antigua or St Lucia? Experience the serene beauty and luxuries of the Leeward Islands.

The stunning Leeward islands of the Caribbean provide an excellent opportunity to enjoy a leisurely cruise amidst secluded tranquility. This route from Antigua to St Lucia provides time to really discover some breath-taking places as you explore this incredible yacht charter destination.

With so many different islands, it would take a very long time to fully discover all of the delightful Leeward Islands. Variety abounds with coral reefs, marine parks and swathes of perfect beaches featuring heavily. Antigua or St Lucia? Both are exceptional in their ways. Snorkelling and diving here are sublime as the underwater world is teeming with marine life. The mild climate and cool constant winds in the Leewards offer some of the best blue-water cruising in the world.

stops.heading: antigua to guadeloupe
stops.text: Embark at Falmouth Harbour on the north west side of the western island. Cruise from here to Guadaloupe and find a sheltered anchorage of choice, where you can enjoy views of the surrounding mountains, lush rain forests and vibrant towns. This is a great area for snorkeling with colourful underwater life amidst crystalline waters. Guadeloupe’s two main islands form the shape of butterfly wings, joined only by bridges and a mangrove swamp. Grand Terre has fabulous beaches teaming with activities and Basse Terre is home to the Parc National, boasting the incredible La Soufriere volcano. Overnight at Deshais Harbour.

stops.heading: guadeloupe
stops.text: In the morning, make way to Isles des Saint’s, a group of islands on the southern end of Guadeloupe with a choice of 2 main anchorages. There is Bourg des Saints on the main island in front of the town and shops, or alternatively, Islet a Cabrit offers a quieter, sheltered anchorage on one of the smaller islands. Both are great places to really enjoy some relaxation while you swim and snorkel the day away.

stops.heading: guadeloupe to dominica
stops.text: Prince Rupert’s Bay is a large natural harbour, set on the northwestern part of the island. It is a great idea to book an organized, guided boat tour up the Indian River surrounded by the rainforest teeming with wildlife. In addition, there is a large town to explore, some great places to snorkel and taking time to simply soak up the atmosphere.

stops.heading: dominica to martinique
stops.text: After breakfast, head to Fort de France for customs clearance then locate a suitable anchorage across from the harbor, near the beach at Anse a L’ane (there is a good choice of places). There are picturesque towns and swathes of velvet beaches ashore. Snorkeling is very good on the outer reefs thanks to the wonderful marine flora and fauna biodiversity.

stops.heading: martinique to st lucia
stops.text: Make way to Marigot Bay and enjoy the sheer tranquility of this beautiful St Lucia yacht charter location. If you head ashore there are some outstanding seafood restaurants or perhaps visit the dive centre at Marigot Beach Club for a fantastic underwater adventure. After lunch, nearby Soufriere, is small town scattered with brightly painted buildings and a bustling seafront. Home to the Diamond Botanical Gardens, this former plantation is bursting with ornamental plants, a waterfall plus geothermal mineral baths. Further inland the cascading Toraille Waterfall is an amazing sight. Anchor overnight near the famous Pitons, which are spectacular volcanic mountain twin peaks.

stops.heading: the pitons to vieux fort
stops.text: Take time to soak up the scenery and explore the Pitons, this world heritage site offers some fantastic walks plus a range of superb diving and snorkeling. Gros Piton, the loftier of the two peaks is climbable for keen hikers and truly affords an ultimate vantage point to view the island. Alternatively, if you are feeling adventurous, a trip by island buggy, a Segway tour or rainforest ziplining can be great fun and will likely cover areas you would not otherwise see. Make way in the evening to Vieux Fort and spend the night in harbour.

stops.heading: vieux fort
stops.text: Situated at the southern end of the island, enjoy the approaching view of mountain ranges and long white sandy beaches plus this area is great for wind and kitesurfing should the mood take you. Perhaps head ashore to Moule a Chique, scenic point, to take advantage of the 360 vistas from this high point. Cruise round to Anse des Sables Beach and drop anchor to enjoy lunch. Disembark at your leisure – Hewanorra International Airport is nearby.

caribbean/virgin-islands/british-virgin-.title: Tortola to Tortola
intro: A yacht charter in the BVI is hard to beat. With over 60 islands in close proximity, it’s an ideal cruising ground for first-time charterers, young families, couples, and seasoned sailors alike.

The shallow waters and short distances between islands allow for easy island hopping, while the BVI’s numerous protected bays provide calm sea conditions even when winds pick up in other Caribbean regions. Whether you’re exploring pristine beaches, indulging in world-class snorkelling and diving, or enjoying a vibrant beach club scene, this 10-day itinerary through the British Virgin Islands offers a mix of relaxation, adventure, and discovery for everyone.

From savouring freshly caught lobster on a secluded beach in Anegada to diving among vibrant coral reefs, each day brings new opportunities to experience the laid-back luxury of the BVI. Thanks to the region’s sheltered waters, you can enjoy smooth cruising throughout your journey, making this a perfect choice for those seeking a seamless island-hopping experience.

stops.heading: Tortola
stops.text: Board your yacht at the picturesque Soper’s Hole Marina. Take a stroll through this colourful harbour, dotted with quaint shops and restaurants like Pusser’s Landing, or venture to Road Town. Here, you can explore the lively streets, sampling local flavours like curried goat and fried conch at one of the seafood shacks. For those looking to stretch their legs, hiking Mount Sage—a 543-metre volcanic peak—offers breathtaking views and a rainforest teeming with wildlife including vocal tree frogs. Anchor in Tortola overnight for a relaxed start to your BVI yacht charter.

stops.heading: Tortola to Norman Island
stops.text: Cruise to Norman Island, famous for its ties to Robert Louis Stevenson’s Treasure Island. Anchor in The Bright, a serene bay perfect for swimming and snorkelling. The adventurous can take the tender to Treasure Point to explore the mysterious sea caves, home to schools of colourful fish. For even more snorkelling, head to Pelican Island and The Indians, where coral gardens teem with marine life. As the sun begins to set, indulge in cocktails at Willy T's—a floating bar known for its lively atmosphere—or dine at Pirates Bight Bar, enjoying a tranquil sunset over the bay.

stops.heading: Norman Island to Peter Island
stops.text: For a day of watersports and relaxation anchor at Little Harbour or Deadman’s Bay, a secluded stretch of soft sand bordered by lush tropical hills. Ashore, visit the Oceans7 Beach Club or indulge in a meal at Deadman’s Bay Beach Bar. For a touch more extravagance, dock at Peter Island Resort in Sprat Bay where world-class wellness and dining facilities await. Their 10,000 sq. ft. spa offers seven luxurious indoor treatment rooms and the resort’s fitness centre is housed in two oceanfront bohios, where you can work out with spectacular views of Big Reef Bay.

stops.heading: Peter Island To Salt, Cooper, And Beef Islands
stops.text: Dive the legendary wreck of the RMS Rhone. Explore the remains of this British mail steamer, which sank in 1867, and swim among the sea life that now calls this historic wreck home. After your dive, cruise to Cooper Island, where you can enjoy lunch at Cooper Island Beach Club, known for its charming atmosphere and local boutiques. Late afternoon, head to your overnight anchorage at Beef Island for cocktails at The Last Resort, a hidden gem set on Bellamy Cay, an islet stranded in the middle of Trellis Bay.

stops.heading: Trellis Bay to Virgin Gorda
stops.text: Cruise to the iconic Baths on Virgin Gorda where giant granite boulders, create spectacle of tidal pools, tunnels, and grottos. Spend the morning wandering through this maze of rocks before hiking to the Top of The Baths restaurant for lunch. In the afternoon, dock at the Bitter End Yacht Club in Gorda Sound, a hub for watersports. Enjoy paddleboarding, windsurfing, or kayaking in the calm waters before a relaxed evening with cocktails on board or ashore at Saba Rock.

stops.heading: Virgin Gorda To Guana Island Or Anegada
stops.text: Cruise to Guana Island, an unspoiled private island that offers complete seclusion. Anchor in White Bay, where you can enjoy a private beach BBQ prepared by your yacht’s chef, or swim in the clear, turquoise waters that surround this pristine location. For a different adventure, weather permitting, head to Anegada—a low-lying coral island famous for its lobster bakes and incredible flats fishing. Here, the island’s uninhabited stretches of beach and local seafood create a sense of true escapism.

stops.heading: Guana Island To Great Camanoe
stops.text: From Guana Island sail to privately owned Great Camanoe. Anchor at Lee Bay, and step ashore to enjoy a private beach picnic prepared by your yacht’s chef, before exploring nearby Cam Bay National Park, where the protected waters host vibrant coral reefs and an array of tropical fish. Birdwatchers will also appreciate the migratory shorebirds that frequent the area. For a more active adventure, hike the island’s nature trails for sweeping views of Scrub Island and Beef Island in the distance. Return to your yacht for sunset cocktails and a special meal under the stars.

stops.heading: Guana Island to Jost Van Dyke
stops.text: Jost Van Dyke, a perennial favourite in the BVI oozes island charm. Anchor in Great Harbour, where beach bars like Foxy’s serve up fresh seafood and rum punch alongside live calypso music. For those seeking adventure, neighbouring Little Jost Van Dyke offers pristine snorkelling and calm waters to explore from the tender. After a day of soaking up the sun, head to the famous Soggy Dollar Bar in White Bay for a signature painkiller cocktail and some island storytelling.

stops.heading: Jost Van Dyke to Tortola
stops.text: After breakfast, enjoy a final swim or paddle board before setting sail for Cane Garden Bay, Tortola’s most famous beach. Known for its lively bars and soft, palm-fringed sands. Drop anchor and spend the day exploring the area—whether relaxing on the beach, enjoying watersports, or taking a tender to Brewers Bay for snorkelling and a scenic hike. For a taste of local culture, visit Callwood Rum Distillery, one of the oldest rum distilleries in the Caribbean, where you can sample the island’s traditional spirits.

stops.heading: Return To Sopers Hole Marina, Tortola
stops.text: After nine days full of exploration return to Soper’s Hole Marina, where you’ll disembark after an unforgettable 10-day journey. Take some time to explore the marina’s local shops or enjoy a waterfront dinner before bidding farewell to your crew and the British Virgin Islands.

caribbean/virgin-islands/british-virgin-.teaser: Whether you’re exploring pristine beaches, indulging in world-class snorkelling and diving, or enjoying a vibrant beach club scene, this 10-day itinerary through the British Virgin Islands offers a mix of relaxation, adventure, and discovery for everyone.

caribbean/virgin-islands/british-virgin-.title: St. Thomas to St. Thomas
intro: The U.S. Virgin Islands, a year-round destination, offer some of the finest cruising grounds in the Caribbean, making them firm favourite for superyacht charters.
With calm waters, beautiful beaches, and rich marine life, the region is ideal for both seasoned charterers and newcomers seeking a unique luxury experience.

This seven-day itinerary showcases the finest of the USVI, from the lively ports of St. Thomas to the pristine, protected bays of St. John, blending adventure with relaxation. You’ll find endless opportunities for snorkelling, diving, and hiking, all within the serenity and privacy of the islands’ sheltered anchorages. Every day brings a new discovery, whether it’s exploring untouched coral reefs or enjoying a beachside meal at a local restaurant. For those seeking a balance of luxury, nature, and adventure, this Caribbean itinerary offers a perfect blend.

stops.heading: St. Thomas to Magens Bay
stops.text: Begin your adventure at Yacht Haven Grande Marina in St. Thomas. After boarding your yacht, cruise to one of the Caribbean’s most picturesque beaches, Magens Bay. Named one of the Top 10 Best Beaches by USA Today, and featured in famous films like The Twilight Saga, Magens Bay is a must visit. Enjoy watersports and stroll along the expansive stretch of soft sand or enjoy a refreshing swim in the clear, shallow waters. As the day winds down, relax on deck while your personal chef prepares some local flavours such as curried goat, fried conch or johnny cakes with views of the lush hills surrounding the bay as your backdrop. This beautiful setting will be your peaceful home for the night.

stops.heading: Magens Bay to Botany Bay
stops.text: After a morning swim in Magens Bay, cruise along St. Thomas's scenic north coast to Botany Bay, a pristine and secluded spot on the island's western tip. Anchor near Sandy Bay Beach, an idyllic setting for a private beach setup and barbecue. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon with freshly prepared local dishes like grilled lobster or jerk chicken. For a touch of adventure, take a short hike to Mermaid’s Chair, where the Atlantic meets the Caribbean in a unique strip of sand. Relax on deck as the sun sets over this quiet haven, soaking in the tranquil beauty before an overnight stay in this serene anchorage.

stops.heading: Botany Bay to Francis Bay, St. John (via Lovango and Congo Cut)
stops.text: A leisurely cruise to Lovango and Congo Cut will present opportunities for daytime hiking and a decadent lunch at Lovango Beach Club. After lunch head to your overnight anchorage at Francis Bay. Located within the U.S. Virgin Islands National Park, this spot is famous for its pristine beaches and abundant sea turtles. Spend late afternoon snorkelling, swimming, or relaxing on deck, and if you’re up for an adventure, take an early morning hike with spectacular views of the island. The peaceful surroundings and natural beauty make this the perfect anchorage for the night.

stops.heading: Francis Bay to Cruz Bay and Waterlemon Cay
stops.text: Cruise to Waterlemon Cay, where you’ll take the tender ashore to Cruz Bay, St. John’s main port and vibrant social hub. Here, enjoy a leisurely afternoon exploring chic boutiques and local shops before returning to Waterlemon Cay, one of the premier snorkelling sites in the U.S. Virgin Islands. The calm, shallow waters around the cay are perfect for snorkellers of all levels, revealing a lively marine world filled with sea turtles, rays, and colourful reef fish. For a dose of history, a short hike from the beach leads to the ruins of an 18th-century Danish plantation, adding a fascinating cultural dimension to this idyllic spot. End your day unwinding on board, surrounded by the beauty of this natural haven.

stops.heading: Waterlemon Cay to Coral Bay
stops.text: Cruise to Round Bay, a gem on the St John's quiet east coast. The bay is perfect for water sports, from paddleboarding to kayaking, or simply enjoying the serenity of this lesser-known anchorage. Take the tender to explore nearby Coral Bay, a laid-back, local town with a charming blend of casual beach bars, small boutiques, and art galleries. A short cruise will bring you to Hurricane Hole, a protected area within the Virgin Islands Coral Reef National Monument. Known for its rich biodiversity, the mangrove-lined shorelines of Hurricane Hole offer incredible snorkelling, with hidden nurseries for juvenile fish and marine creatures.

stops.heading: Coral Bay to Reef Bay
stops.text: Departing Coral Bay, set a course for Reef Bay, a secluded haven on St. John's southern coast. Upon arrival, anchor near the historic Reef Bay Sugar Mill Ruins, a testament to the island's 19th-century sugar production era. Accessible via a short hike from the beach, these well-preserved ruins offer a glimpse into the island's colonial past. For snorkelling enthusiasts, the nearby waters around Ditleff Point present vibrant coral formations and diverse marine life, providing an underwater adventure in a tranquil setting. As evening approaches, enjoy the serene ambiance of Reef Bay, surrounded by lush hills and the gentle sounds of the Caribbean Sea, making it an ideal spot for a spectacular dinner on board and a peaceful overnight anchorage.

stops.heading: Reef Bay to Honeymoon Beach and Disembark at Charlotte Amalie
stops.text: After a relaxing breakfast, set off for Honeymoon Beach, a picture-perfect cove known for its pristine sands and gentle, turquoise waters. Spend the morning soaking up the sun, swimming, or taking a scenic hike along the Lind Point Trail, where tropical foliage and coastal views create an idyllic backdrop for a final island adventure. After lunch, cruise back to St. Thomas, arriving at Charlotte Amalie by midday. Here, take in the vibrant sights of the island’s bustling town, with time for some last-minute shopping or a leisurely waterfront lunch. Conclude your unforgettable journey at Yacht Haven Grande Marina, where your crew will bid you a warm farewell.

caribbean/virgin-islands/us-virgin-islan.title: Tortola to Tortola
intro: A yacht charter in the BVI is hard to beat. With over 60 islands in close proximity, it’s an ideal cruising ground for first-time charterers, young families, couples, and seasoned sailors alike.

The shallow waters and short distances between islands allow for easy island hopping, while the BVI’s numerous protected bays provide calm sea conditions even when winds pick up in other Caribbean regions. Whether you’re exploring pristine beaches, indulging in world-class snorkelling and diving, or enjoying a vibrant beach club scene, this 10-day itinerary through the British Virgin Islands offers a mix of relaxation, adventure, and discovery for everyone.

From savouring freshly caught lobster on a secluded beach in Anegada to diving among vibrant coral reefs, each day brings new opportunities to experience the laid-back luxury of the BVI. Thanks to the region’s sheltered waters, you can enjoy smooth cruising throughout your journey, making this a perfect choice for those seeking a seamless island-hopping experience.

stops.heading: Tortola
stops.text: Board your yacht at the picturesque Soper’s Hole Marina. Take a stroll through this colourful harbour, dotted with quaint shops and restaurants like Pusser’s Landing, or venture to Road Town. Here, you can explore the lively streets, sampling local flavours like curried goat and fried conch at one of the seafood shacks. For those looking to stretch their legs, hiking Mount Sage—a 543-metre volcanic peak—offers breathtaking views and a rainforest teeming with wildlife including vocal tree frogs. Anchor in Tortola overnight for a relaxed start to your BVI yacht charter.

stops.heading: Tortola to Norman Island
stops.text: Cruise to Norman Island, famous for its ties to Robert Louis Stevenson’s Treasure Island. Anchor in The Bright, a serene bay perfect for swimming and snorkelling. The adventurous can take the tender to Treasure Point to explore the mysterious sea caves, home to schools of colourful fish. For even more snorkelling, head to Pelican Island and The Indians, where coral gardens teem with marine life. As the sun begins to set, indulge in cocktails at Willy T's—a floating bar known for its lively atmosphere—or dine at Pirates Bight Bar, enjoying a tranquil sunset over the bay.

stops.heading: Norman Island to Peter Island
stops.text: For a day of watersports and relaxation anchor at Little Harbour or Deadman’s Bay, a secluded stretch of soft sand bordered by lush tropical hills. Ashore, visit the Oceans7 Beach Club or indulge in a meal at Deadman’s Bay Beach Bar. For a touch more extravagance, dock at Peter Island Resort in Sprat Bay where world-class wellness and dining facilities await. Their 10,000 sq. ft. spa offers seven luxurious indoor treatment rooms and the resort’s fitness centre is housed in two oceanfront bohios, where you can work out with spectacular views of Big Reef Bay.

stops.heading: Peter Island To Salt, Cooper, And Beef Islands
stops.text: Dive the legendary wreck of the RMS Rhone. Explore the remains of this British mail steamer, which sank in 1867, and swim among the sea life that now calls this historic wreck home. After your dive, cruise to Cooper Island, where you can enjoy lunch at Cooper Island Beach Club, known for its charming atmosphere and local boutiques. Late afternoon, head to your overnight anchorage at Beef Island for cocktails at The Last Resort, a hidden gem set on Bellamy Cay, an islet stranded in the middle of Trellis Bay.

stops.heading: Trellis Bay to Virgin Gorda
stops.text: Cruise to the iconic Baths on Virgin Gorda where giant granite boulders, create spectacle of tidal pools, tunnels, and grottos. Spend the morning wandering through this maze of rocks before hiking to the Top of The Baths restaurant for lunch. In the afternoon, dock at the Bitter End Yacht Club in Gorda Sound, a hub for watersports. Enjoy paddleboarding, windsurfing, or kayaking in the calm waters before a relaxed evening with cocktails on board or ashore at Saba Rock.

stops.heading: Virgin Gorda To Guana Island Or Anegada
stops.text: Cruise to Guana Island, an unspoiled private island that offers complete seclusion. Anchor in White Bay, where you can enjoy a private beach BBQ prepared by your yacht’s chef, or swim in the clear, turquoise waters that surround this pristine location. For a different adventure, weather permitting, head to Anegada—a low-lying coral island famous for its lobster bakes and incredible flats fishing. Here, the island’s uninhabited stretches of beach and local seafood create a sense of true escapism.

stops.heading: Guana Island To Great Camanoe
stops.text: From Guana Island sail to privately owned Great Camanoe. Anchor at Lee Bay, and step ashore to enjoy a private beach picnic prepared by your yacht’s chef, before exploring nearby Cam Bay National Park, where the protected waters host vibrant coral reefs and an array of tropical fish. Birdwatchers will also appreciate the migratory shorebirds that frequent the area. For a more active adventure, hike the island’s nature trails for sweeping views of Scrub Island and Beef Island in the distance. Return to your yacht for sunset cocktails and a special meal under the stars.

stops.heading: Guana Island to Jost Van Dyke
stops.text: Jost Van Dyke, a perennial favourite in the BVI oozes island charm. Anchor in Great Harbour, where beach bars like Foxy’s serve up fresh seafood and rum punch alongside live calypso music. For those seeking adventure, neighbouring Little Jost Van Dyke offers pristine snorkelling and calm waters to explore from the tender. After a day of soaking up the sun, head to the famous Soggy Dollar Bar in White Bay for a signature painkiller cocktail and some island storytelling.

stops.heading: Jost Van Dyke to Tortola
stops.text: After breakfast, enjoy a final swim or paddle board before setting sail for Cane Garden Bay, Tortola’s most famous beach. Known for its lively bars and soft, palm-fringed sands. Drop anchor and spend the day exploring the area—whether relaxing on the beach, enjoying watersports, or taking a tender to Brewers Bay for snorkelling and a scenic hike. For a taste of local culture, visit Callwood Rum Distillery, one of the oldest rum distilleries in the Caribbean, where you can sample the island’s traditional spirits.

stops.heading: Return To Sopers Hole Marina, Tortola
stops.text: After nine days full of exploration return to Soper’s Hole Marina, where you’ll disembark after an unforgettable 10-day journey. Take some time to explore the marina’s local shops or enjoy a waterfront dinner before bidding farewell to your crew and the British Virgin Islands.

mediterranean/croatia/dubrovnik.title: Dubrovnik to Trogir
intro: Explore gorgeous backdrops and exciting sailing along the coastline of Croatia. The stunning beaches, secluded coves and traditional villages are all best accessed by superyacht.

From Dubrovnik to Trogir, take in some of the stunning shorelines in Croatia. From the green expanse of relaxed Mljet to the bustle of historic Hvar, there are countless towns, beaches and national parks for charterers to enjoy.

stops.heading: dubrovnik
stops.text: The best known sailing destination in Croatia, Dubrovnik is a beautifully preserved city with a distinctive Old Town encircled by massive stone walls. The well-preserved buildings range from Baroque St. Blaise Church to Renaissance Sponza Palace and Gothic Rector’s Palace. Anchor and explore the cultural attractions.

stops.heading: mljet
stops.text: The beautiful island of Mljet, with its relaxed Mediterranean atmosphere, is a perfect first stop on your cruise. The Croatian Islands are renowned for scenic saltwater lakes and pristine waters. Try out your yacht’s water toys.

stops.heading: vis
stops.text: Vis is a superlative island with a stunning blue grotto, peaceful, deserted beaches, vineyard blanketed hills and olive groves. Go ashore for a walk through the dense greenery.

stops.heading: hvar
stops.text: Don’t miss the chance to visit Hvar, well known for its welcoming locals as well as its myriad historical and cultural sights. Effusive in the summer, peaceful and idyllic in the winter, Hvar is a fantastic island always erring on the side of sophistication.

stops.heading: brac
stops.text: Enjoy Croatia’s most popular beach, Bol, on the coast of Brac. Here you can relax, sunbathe and enjoy the water sports from snorkelling to windsurfing.

stops.heading: split
stops.text: Anchor in the welcoming seaport of Split with its picturesque old town. Explore the emperor Diocletian’s palace and wander through the cosmopolitan streets enjoying the fine dining and dynamic energy as the town comes into its own at night.

stops.heading: trogir
stops.text: The final stop, Trogir, is an ideal place to end your charter. Watch the sunset while sipping cocktails at one of the many romantic bars along the coastline.

mediterranean/croatia/dubrovnik.title: Split to Dubrovnik
intro: Seven days on the Dalmatian coast moves through some of the most varied sailing in the Adriatic: a UNESCO-listed Roman palace, an island that spent four decades as a closed military zone, pine forests reaching the water's edge, and the medieval walls of Dubrovnik at the end of it.

This Croatia yacht charter itinerary runs Split to Dubrovnik via Maslinica, Vis, Hvar, Korčula, Mljet and Šipan, covering the central and southern Dalmatian coast at a pace that leaves time to actually be in each place.

Croatia has over 1,200 islands along its Adriatic coastline. Most charter guests never need more than a dozen of them. There are plenty of reasons to charter in Croatia beyond this single route, but the itinerary below covers the best of the central and south Dalmatian islands in seven days, with a clearly optional extension into Montenegro for those who want more.

stops.heading: Split and Maslinica
stops.text: Embarkation is in Split. The morning before embarkation goes to Diocletian’s Palace, a Roman emperor’s retirement complex built in the fourth century and now the living heart of Split’s Old Town, with restaurants, bars and apartments occupying the original imperial apartments and mausoleum. It’s one of the better-preserved Roman structures in Europe and worth the hour ashore before the yacht slips its lines. The cruise to Maslinica takes around an hour. Sitting on the western tip of Šolta island, Maslinica is one of the most sheltered anchorages in central Dalmatia: a small harbour village overlooked by the eighteenth-century Martinis Marchi castle on its own islet at the bay’s entrance, with olive groves running back into the hills behind. The waterfront has a handful of excellent restaurants, and the pace is noticeably slower than Split. Dinner ashore or on board, with a walk out to the castle islet for those who want the view back over the bay at sunset.

stops.heading: Maslinica to Vis
stops.text: The morning is unhurried, with time to explore Maslinica’s waterfront and, tide and appetite allowing, a swim in one of the coves nearby before the yacht heads for Vis. Vis is the furthest inhabited island from the Croatian mainland, and the quietest stop on the route. It was closed to all foreign visitors from the late 1940s until 1989, used as a major Yugoslav naval base with over 20 kilometres of underground tunnels carved into the island’s interior. That isolation preserved it. The fishing villages, the food, the landscape and the pace of life on Vis feel noticeably different from the islands that have had decades of tourism to contend with. Stern to in Vis town for a fascinating tour of the underground tunnels with a local guide, before heading south. Enjoy an afternoon tender ride around the coast before the yacht docks in Komiža Bay on the southwest side of the island, a small fishing village with a harbour full of traditional wooden boats. Komiža has some excellent lobster restaurants, perfect for a dinner ashore.

stops.heading: The Pakleni Islands and Hvar
stops.text: Komiža gets one last unhurried look before the yacht heads for Hvar, with the afternoon spent at anchor in the Pakleni Islands, the scatter of pine-covered islets just off Hvar that offer some of the best swimming and watersports on the route. Lunch on board, tenders in the water. The tender ride into Hvar Town in the afternoon takes minutes. Hvar has a reputation for nightlife and beach clubs, and the main square delivers on both if that is what the group wants. It is also genuinely beautiful, and the views from the old fortress above the town over the Pakleni Islands and out to the open Adriatic are worth the climb alone. Anchor overnight in the islands or in the harbour.

stops.heading: Hvar to Korčula
stops.text: The morning belongs to Hvar before the yacht moves on. Korčula is described as Little Dubrovnik for its medieval stone architecture, its walls and towers and the density of its old town crammed onto a small peninsula. It’s also claimed, with varying levels of evidence, as the birthplace of Marco Polo. The old town is worth an evening: dinner ashore in one of the restaurants in the old walls, with the Adriatic on three sides. The passage takes between 3-4 hours, depending on conditions. The yacht anchors for lunch at a bay on the way across, chosen on the day.

stops.heading: Korčula to Mljet National Park
stops.text: Mljet is the green island, and one of Croatia’s truly beautiful national parks. Dense pine and oak forests run to the water’s edge, and the national park in the western third of the island contains two saltwater lakes connected by a channel, Malo Jezero and Veliko Jezero, surrounded by woodland with a small Benedictine monastery sitting on an island in the larger lake. The yacht stern-ties among the trees, lunch on board, and the afternoon is on foot: a walk through the pine forest to Veliko Jezero, a boat trip to the monastery, a swim in the lake. Dinner on board as the light drops into the forest. The passage from Korčula takes around two hours. Mljet National Park requires an entry fee, paid on arrival.

stops.heading: Mljet to Šipan
stops.text: A last morning in Mljet National Park before the yacht heads for the Elaphiti Islands, the small archipelago scattered southwest of Dubrovnik. Šipan is the largest of the group and the quietest: no cars, no crowds, just olive groves, old stone farmhouses, and a scatter of ruined summer villas built by Dubrovnik’s nobility, who used the island as a retreat from the city for centuries. The yacht ties up in Šipanska Luka, the main village on the island’s southwestern coast, where a scatter of restaurants line the small harbour. The afternoon is unhurried: a walk up through the olive terraces, a swim off the yacht, or simply time on deck watching the light change over the bay. Dinner ashore at one of the harbourside restaurants, or on board if the group prefers to stay put.

stops.heading: Šipan to Dubrovnik: Disembark
stops.text: The final passage is short, around an hour and a half, and brings the yacht into Dubrovnik itself. The tender ride into the Old Town takes only minutes from the anchorage: the medieval walls, the Stradun, the Rector’s Palace and the cable car to the top of Mount Srđ for the view over the walled city and the Adriatic beyond. Final breakfast on board, with time for a last look at Dubrovnik’s Old Town before disembarkation. Or, for those who want to continue, the optional Montenegro extension begins here.

stops.heading: Optional Extension: Montenegro
stops.text: Guests wishing to extend into Montenegro should note that departing Croatian waters at Dubrovnik requires a formal customs clearance. This isn’t a complex process but it needs to be planned in advance with the Captain. It isn’t a simple continuation of the same cruise. The passage from Dubrovnik to Kotor takes between 2-3 hours. Kotor sits deep into the Bay of Kotor, a deep fjord-like inlet in the Montenegrin coast, with a walled old town and mountains rising steeply behind it. Day 8 continues to Portonovi, with the Aman resort available for dinner or a spa visit. Day 9 runs the Montenegro coast to Budva or directly to Tivat for departure, depending on the group’s schedule.
